speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 但我认为我们这样表述是为了强迫自己记住，你不仅仅为了招聘而招聘产品经理，你是在有真正特定需求的地方招聘一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think what goes with it, Lenny, is you have to build the culture of the organization around that.
zh: 我认为随之而来的是，Lenny，你必须围绕这一点建立组织文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for example, when we say we regret product management exists, every time we write documents about how we ship or what we're doing, we're very clear that anyone can bring change forward, that we can have DRIs of new product development that is an engineer or is a designer, but that everybody goes through that same level of function of you've got to go through product review, you've got to actually do the work because it is real work.
zh: 所以举个例子，当说我们后悔产品管理存在时，每次我们撰写关于如何发布或我们在做什么的文档时，我们都非常清楚，任何人都可以提出变更，我们可以有作为工程师或设计师的新产品开发 DRI，但每个人都经历同样级别的职能，你必须通过产品评审，你必须实际做这项工作，因为这是真正的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if people don't want to do that, if they want to do something else, we can always move product management around.
zh: 如果人们不想做这个，如果他们想做别的事情，我们总是可以重新调配产品管理。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so rather than mapping PMs to teams where you assume that the PM will always do that, we tend to map them to problems or core projects.
zh: 因此，与其将产品经理映射到团队，假设产品经理总是会做这些，我们倾向于将他们映射到问题或核心项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that means that there will be a year more where there isn't a PM attached to a particular engineering team, even though there's lots of ongoing product work to do.
zh: 这意味着会有整整一年没有产品经理附着在特定的工程团队上，尽管有大量的持续产品工作要做。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I love about this is we often hear people at eng-oriented products talk like this, like developer tools where we don't need PMs.
zh: 我喜欢这一点，我们经常听到在以工程为导向的产品中的人这样说话，比如开发者工具，我们不需要产品经理。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why do we need PMs?
zh: 为什么我们需要产品经理？

speaker: Unknown
en: And it often comes from companies like Linear, companies that are building developer tools where you could see why engineers are enough.
zh: 这通常来自像 Linear 这样的公司，正在构建开发者工具的公司，在那里你可以明白为什么工程师就够了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's really interesting to hear from your perspective because you've built very consumery products, very, very consumery products that require what you think are very strong PM skills.
zh: 所以从你的角度听到这些真的很有趣，因为你构建了非常面向消费者的产品，非常非常面向消费者的产品，这需要你认为很强的产品经理技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it means a lot, but even more so coming from you that you find that PMs aren't as necessary as people may think in building something great.
zh: 所以这意味着很多，但特别是从你这里说出来更有意义，因为你发现产品经理并不像人们认为的那样在构建伟大的东西时是必要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think there was two parts that drove it.
zh: 是的，我认为有两个部分推动了它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I've certainly, a lot of what I'm talking about here are things that I've definitely learned over time.
zh: 我当然，我在这里谈论的很多事情绝对是我随着时间学到的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I spent seven years at Twitch prior to time at Whatnot, and that was very Amazon two pizza team ratio driven.
zh: 我在加入 Whatnot 之前在 Twitch 度过了七年，那是非常亚马逊两个披萨团队比例驱动的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I started in the Valley at Twitter and that was similarly very like you always had this kind of very tight alignment, and God, there was a lot of alignment meetings, so you can imagine why engineers didn't want to be in them.
zh: 我在硅谷从 Twitter 开始，那同样非常像你总是有这种非常紧密的一致性，天哪，有大量的一致性会议，所以你可以想象为什么工程师不想参加它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's kind of evolved over time to understand that actually a lot of that is just a function of management not being able to see what's going on.
zh: 随着时间的推移，这有点演变成了理解实际上其中很多只是管理层无法看到正在发生的事情的功能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you hire more folks and you build more layers and your systems beget systems.
zh: 所以你雇佣更多人，你建立更多层级，你的系统产生系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think what's really changing is people are realizing that it's not true anymore that the only way to get leverage is just to hire more PMs underneath you and be more senior, that we've got a better understanding of what's happening in businesses now.
zh: 我认为真正改变的是人们意识到，不再是为了获得杠杆作用的唯一方法就是在你下面雇佣更多的产品经理并更资深，我们现在对商业中发生的事情有了更好的理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's easier to converse directly with the code base and talk to engineers than it ever has been.
zh: 直接与代码库对话并与工程师交谈比以往任何时候都容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you don't actually have to get into this all scale thing.
zh: 所以你实际上不必进入这种全规模的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I don't really think consumer or enterprise is the cutting point anymore.
zh: 我真的不认为消费者或企业是分界点了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's more the culture of the organization itself.
zh: 我认为更多的是组织本身的文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: How much of this shift in your mind is AI driven because AI now enables non-PMs to do PME work?
zh: 在你看来这种转变有多少是 AI 驱动的，因为 AI 现在使非产品经理能够做产品经理的工作？

speaker: Unknown
en: And how much of it was pre-AI?
zh: 有多少是在 AI 之前的？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I want to talk about just what this actually looks like in your team, but let me ask that question first.
zh: 然后我想谈谈这在你的团队中实际上是什么样的，但让我先问那个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think it's explicitly because of AI, but I do think AI makes it a lot easier.
zh: 我认为这不明确是因为 AI，但我认为 AI 使它容易得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's two things.
zh: 我认为有两件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think AI certainly means that there's an enormous amount of leverage for an IC.
zh: 我认为 AI 当然意味着个体贡献者有巨大的杠杆作用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, I don't know how much other people feel this, but I was talking to a couple of our senior leads the other day, and we feel that we're so capable of doing things now with AI that you almost feel a bunch of pressure of the stuff you're not doing because you know that if you carved out a couple more hours, you could move a lot of stuff.
zh: 现在，我不知道有多少其他人有这种感觉，但我前几天和我们的一些高级负责人谈话，我们感觉到我们现在非常有能力用 AI 做事，你几乎会感觉到一堆关于你没有做的事情的压力，因为你知道如果你腾出更多几个小时，你可以移动很多东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's certainly easier to move fast with AI tooling if you've got well-honed judgment.
zh: 如果你有磨练得很好的判断力，用 AI 工具快速移动当然更容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can pull data now on a Hex thread that is basically what it would take a week, two weeks with an Amazon L7 data scientist in 2017.
zh: 你现在可以在一个 Hex 线程中提取数据，这基本上是 2017 年的一名亚马逊 L7 数据科学家需要一周，两周的工作量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you're empowered and have good judgment, you can basically make really quick decisions and just keep people moving, which is extraordinary.
zh: 所以如果你被赋予权力并有良好的判断力，你基本上可以做出非常快的决定并只是让人们保持移动，这是非凡的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But more than just AI, I think it's also a lot of those ratio pushes also came with a bunch of other cultural pushes like hire great people and get out of their way, bottoms up roadmaps, and all of those pieces where I think there's been a bit of a cultural shift in tech over the last little while, which is like actually top-down's pretty good because folks at the top, generally speaking, can make quick decisions and remove all of this alignment debate.
zh: 但除了 AI 之外，我认为很多这些比例推动也伴随着一系列其他文化推动，比如雇佣优秀的人并不要阻碍他们，自下而上的路线图，以及所有这些部分，我认为在最近的一段时间里科技界有了一点文化转变，这就像实际上自上而下相当不错，因为顶层的人，一般来说，可以做出快速的决定并消除所有这些一致性辩论。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have probably more macro context than most folks.
zh: 他们可能比大多数人拥有更多的宏观背景。

speaker: Unknown
en: And assuming that they are genuinely in touch with ground truth and are good enough, it's actually a really efficient model to be able to have senior leadership involved in a lot of those decisions, which means it's not just the tooling that makes them efficient, but you can have one very senior PM across more things and they can be more efficient than having three relatively entry level PMs.
zh: 假设他们真正接触到了地面真相并且足够好，这是一种非常高效的模型，能够让高级领导层参与许多这些决定，这意味着不仅仅是工具使他们高效，但你可以在更多事情上拥有一名非常资深的产品经理，他们可以比拥有三名相对入门级的产品经理更高效。

speaker: Unknown
en: But certainly AI makes all of that a lot easier again.
zh: 但当然 AI 再次使所有这些变得容易得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: So just to coming back to the broad premise, which I think is very important to clarify, this point about regretting product management exists isn't saying we don't want or think PMs are useful.
zh: 所以回到广泛的前提，我认为这很重要要澄清，关于后悔产品管理存在的这一点不是说我们不想要或认为产品经理是有用的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's that it is better to not assume we need a PM in every place.
zh: 这是最好不要假设我们在每个地方都需要产品经理。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it is great to enable other functions to do the PM work.
zh: 而且让其他职能做产品经理的工作是很棒的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also just PMs take away the reps from people being able to do the things that PMs do.
zh: 而且还有产品经理剥夺了人们做产品经理能做的事情的练习机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if they can do that work, they can actually execute better, build better products for people.
zh: 如果他们能做那项工作，他们实际上可以执行得更好，为人们构建更好的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's also better for PMs to not be mapped specifically to a team than it is to say we go where the work is.
zh: 我认为产品经理不专门映射到一个团队，而是说我们跟随工作去的地方，这对产品经理也更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: You will build more and better reps. You can work out more muscle groups by moving around on the things you work on as opposed to saying, I'm attached to whatever this EM owns.
zh: 你将建立更多更好的练习。你可以在你工作的项目上移动来锻炼更多的肌肉群，而不是说，我依附于这个工程经理拥有的任何东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's follow that thread.
zh: 所以让我们跟随这个线索。

speaker: Unknown
en: What does the team look like?
zh: 团队是什么样的？

speaker: Unknown
en: What does the PM/eng design team look like at Whatnot?
zh: 在 Whatnot，产品经理/工程/设计团队是什么样的？

speaker: Unknown
en: What does this org look like in this worldview?
zh: 在这种世界观下，这个组织是什么样的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, we've just passed 20 PMs.
zh: 是的，我们刚刚通过了 20 位 PM。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have, I think 21, 22 PMs in the building today.
zh: 我们今天在大楼里大概有 21、22 位 PM。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which for those following what our trajectory is is pretty small considering the volume of GMV that our sellers move.
zh: 对于那些关注我们轨迹的人来说，考虑到我们的卖家移动的 GMV 总量，这是相当小的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're very loosely organized into three groups, buyer, seller, and what we would call trust and risk.
zh: 我们非常松散地组织成三个组，买家、卖家，以及我们所谓的信任和风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the folks looking after our standards, payments, safety, et cetera.
zh: 所以那些负责我们的标准、支付、安全等的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then within those broad groups, we basically reassign the PMs pretty regularly.
zh: 然后在这些大组内部，我们基本上非常定期地重新分配 PM。

speaker: Unknown
en: So people have loose alignment.
zh: 所以人们有松散的一致性。

speaker: Unknown
en: You might be broadly a growth PM or broadly work on discovery.
zh: 你可能大体上是一个增长 PM 或者大体上在发现上工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: But even amongst those groups, it gets allocated and moved around pretty quickly.
zh: 但即使在那些组中，分配和调动也相当快。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's because the way that we do planning is every six months, the CEO, myself, some other folks and senior leads, will sit down and just define what needs to be true over the next six months.
zh: 这是因为我们做规划的方式是每六个月，CEO、我、一些其他人和资深负责人会坐下来，只是定义接下来的六个月里什么是必须成真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do we have to get done as a company, both in terms of outcomes and critical projects?
zh: 作为一家公司我们必须完成什么，既包括结果也包括关键项目？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we sit down and we go through that list and say, who's the DRI?
zh: 然后我们坐下来，过一遍那个清单，说，谁是 DRI？

speaker: Unknown
en: Who's accountable for that?
zh: 谁对此负责？

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's mostly how we end up allocating PM work.
zh: 这基本上就是我们最终分配 PM 工作的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so quite regularly you'll have something, we've just finished a planning cycle literally this morning, and you'll quite regularly go through those and you'll get to the end and say, "Cool, there's this thing that's second or third priority in a bunch of different teams' roadmaps.
zh: 所以你会经常遇到这种情况，我们今天早上刚完成一个规划周期，你会经常过一遍这些，你会到最后说，“酷，这事儿在不同团队的路标里是第二或第三优先级。

speaker: Unknown
en: That feels really important.
zh: 感觉真的很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who owns that?
zh: 谁拥有这个？

speaker: Unknown
en: We actually don't have an owner for that."
zh: 我们其实没有负责人。"

speaker: Unknown
en: And we'll go and grab a PM and be like, "Congratulations, this is the thing we need you to deliver over the next six months."
zh: 然后我们会去抓一个 PM 说，“恭喜，这是我们接下来六个月需要你去交付的东西。”

speaker: Unknown
en: It's rarely you need to build a feature that works exactly this way, that does this thing.
zh: 极少情况是你需要构建一个功能完全是这样工作的，做这件事的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a little more high level than that.
zh: 它比那稍微高一个层次。

speaker: Unknown
en: But how do you go and work out what needs to be true?
zh: 但你怎么去搞清楚什么必须成真？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you map the human beings that you think can guide that.
zh: 然后你映射你认为可以引导这件事的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not every name is a PM name, but overwhelmingly when you go through that planning process, it tends to be PMs and it tends to be PMs who have the right skillset vis-a-vis what it is, whether it's more financial, whether it's more algorithmic and recommendations-based, whether or not it's core user feature.
zh: 不是每个名字都是 PM 的名字，但绝大多数情况下，当你过那个规划流程时，倾向于 PM，而且倾向于 PM 拥有相对于那个事情的正确技能组合，不管是偏财务，还是偏算法和基于推荐，还是核心用户功能。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me follow that actual specific thread at the end there around what you look for in product managers that you hire.
zh: 让我顺着最后那个具体的线索，关于你在招聘产品经理时看重什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you also wrote this brutal quote, "In the last two years, 31,832 people applied to be a product manager at Whatnot.
zh: 所以你还写了这句残酷的话，“在过去两年里，31,832 人申请成为 Whatnot 的产品经理。

speaker: Unknown
en: We hired one."
zh: 我们录用了 1 个。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, sir.
zh: 是的，先生。

speaker: Lenny
en: Brutal.
zh: 残酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's pretty great.
zh: 很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: Pretty great.
zh: 很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's a few things here I want to talk about.
zh: 所以这里有几件事我想聊聊。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is just what does it you look for in the folks that you hire?
zh: 一个是你招人时看重什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Especially these days, what's trending up in what you find you need in really successful PMs and whatnot?
zh: 特别是这些天，在你发现非常成功的 PM 需要的素质里，什么是趋势向下的？

speaker: Unknown
en: And what's maybe trending down?
zh: 什么是可能趋势向下的？

speaker: Unknown
en: I can tell you what's definitely trending down.
zh: 我可以告诉你什么是肯定趋势向下的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's folks who spend a lot of the time in their interviews talking about those alignment meetings and driving alignment and stakeholder management and those pieces.
zh: 是那些在面试中花很多时间谈论那些对齐会议、推动对齐和利益相关者管理以及这些片段的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because there's definitely a group of PMs, and I certainly used to be one of them earlier in my career, whose specialty wasn't technical or customer-oriented, it was politics.
zh: 因为肯定有一组 PM，我职业生涯早期肯定也是其中之一，他们的特长不是技术或客户导向，是政治。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so folks who tend to naturally lean towards driving alignment, building relationships, tell me about a time when you failed and you're like, "Oh, I didn't keep the CEO up to date with something and that led to a pivot," is definitely a thing that is a bit of an anti-pattern that trends down.
zh: 所以那些天然倾向于推动对齐、建立关系的人，告诉我一次你失败的经历，你会说，“哦，我没有让 CEO 了解某事的进展，导致了转型”，这绝对是一个有点反模式且趋势向下的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: What we tend to find really jumps in a PM kind of interview is, over the course of your interviews or your case study, can we see both the macro thinking and the micro thinking?
zh: 我们倾向于发现真的能让 PM 在面试中脱颖而出的，是在你的面试或案例研究中，我们能同时看到宏观思考和微观思考吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the system works something like this and I can describe an end state, but can I almost exude impatience on, and here's how I would validate that very quickly, here's where I would push to get that done, and are you specific about the things that you've built?
zh: 我认为系统是这样运作的，我可以描述一个最终状态，但我能不能几乎表现出不耐烦，这是我会非常快验证它的方法，这是我会推动去完成它的方法，并且你对构建的东西具体吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's an awful lot of folks who've worked at FANG, Uber, or pick any scale company where they babysat things that existed, and they've maybe polished the edges of it as opposed to the idea of saying, we were given this problem and I had to go and come up with something unique and novel, or I had to really iterate our way through a complicated change.
zh: 有很多人在 FANG、Uber，或者选任何规模化公司工作过，他们在那里照看存在的东西，他们可能只是润色了边缘，而不是说，我们被给了这个问题，我得去想出独特和新颖的东西，或者我真的通过复杂的变化迭代出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I made decisions along the way and we moved.
zh: 但我在路上做了决定，我们推进了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because I think it's easy in a very large organization with inertia to go along with what's happening and not necessarily be an agent of change or be a decision maker, which is ultimately what you need PM to do.
zh: 因为我认为在一个有惯性的大组织里很容易随大流，不一定是变化的智能体或决策者，而这最终是你需要 PM 去做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's something you said there that I just had Elizabeth Stone on the podcast.
zh: 你刚才说了一件事，我刚才邀请 Elizabeth Stone 上播客。

speaker: Unknown
en: She's CPTO at Netflix, and asked her what's the trait that is also most trending up.
zh: 她是 Netflix 的 CPTO，问她什么特性也是趋势向上的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And she said exactly what you said initially, which was the systems thinking, thinking big picture, thinking about the bigger business, and her advice there to work on this, and I want to ask you if you have any other advice here.
zh: 她说的和你刚才开始说的一模一样，就是系统思维，大局思考，思考更大的业务，她关于这方面的建议是，我想问问你有没有其他建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: Say someone hears this, you're like, oh wow, I got to work on my systems thinking skills.
zh: 假设有人听了这个，你就像，哦哇，我得修炼我的系统思维技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: Her advice is take one click back from your problem and think about, okay, for my manager, how do they think about this problem and how does that impact the rest of the business?
zh: 她的建议是从你的问题退后一步，思考，好吧，对于我的老板，他们怎么思考这个问题，这怎么影响业务的其余部分？

speaker: Unknown
en: Thoughts on just how somebody might develop the skill and get better at systems thinking?
zh: 关于某人可能如何培养这种技能并变得更擅长系统思维的想法？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I think the skill is exactly the right way to say it.
zh: 我的意思是，我认为用技能这个词说是完全正确的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you can get good at it from just a mental exercise.
zh: 我认为你可以仅仅通过一种思维练习就变得擅长它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can do it in small ways.
zh: 所以你可以从小处着手。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the things I ask a lot in product review when someone says, "Hey, we want to run an experiment," is, "Okay, what do we do if it's green?
zh: 在产品评审中，当有人说“嘿，我们想做一个实验”时，我经常问的一件事是，“好吧，如果它是绿的，我们做什么？”

speaker: Unknown
en: What do we do if it's red?"
zh: “如果它是红的，我们做什么？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And if folks are like, "Actually, I don't know how my strategy would change."
zh: 如果人们说，“实际上，我不知道我的策略会如何改变。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Cool, we haven't really thought about that.
zh: 酷，我们还没有真正思考过那一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So stop and go and do the mental exercise of how it would work.
zh: 所以停下来，去做那种它会如何运作的思维练习。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I think it's the same thing of you can build quick local solutions if you have done the mental exercise in your head of say, well, what would happen if we had 1,000 times more usage of this than we expected?
zh: 然后我认为这是一样的，如果你在头脑中做过思维练习，你就可以构建快速的本地解决方案，比如说，如果我们有比预期多 1000 倍的使用量会发生什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or what are the unexpected knock-on effects that this could have?
zh: 或者这会有什么意想不到的连锁反应？

speaker: Unknown
en: And how do you just start doing all of that in your head before you get pen on paper, before you get code in the system?
zh: 以及你如何在下笔之前，在把代码写入系统之前，就在头脑中开始做所有这些事情？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it helps actually unblock people to move faster too, because I think the other thing that PMs are often slowed down by is all risk.
zh: 我认为这实际上确实有助于解锁人们的束缚，让他们行动得更快，因为我认为 PM 经常被拖慢的另一个原因是所有的风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, legal might, finance might, another team might.
zh: 哦，法务可能会，财务可能会，另一个团队可能会。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think one of the monikers we use internally is no, then go.
zh: 我认为我们在内部使用的一个口头禅是先说不，再行动。

speaker: Unknown
en: As in just think through all the things that could go wrong, understand where scale will break, understand the things that might happen, and then move on anyway.
zh: 意思是只要想清楚所有可能出错的事情，理解规模会在哪里出问题，理解可能发生的事情，然后无论如何继续前进。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because if you've thought through all the things that could happen at scale, you're probably going to preempt a bunch of them.
zh: 因为如果你已经想清楚了所有在规模上可能发生的事情，你可能会预先解决其中的一大部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I really like Elizabeth's quote there, but mine is just do the mental exercise of just playing out, if it gets really widely adopted, if it happens, if there is something that goes wrong, what will it be?
zh: 所以我真的很喜欢 Elizabeth 在那里的引用，但我的建议是，只是做这种思维练习，只是推演一下，如果它被广泛采用，如果它发生了，如果有东西出错了，那会是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't have to solve all of them.
zh: 你不必解决所有问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've just got to think through all of them and then you end up solving more than you think.
zh: 你只需要把所有问题都过一遍，然后你最终会解决比你想象的更多的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love that.
zh: 我喜欢那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's essentially don't just focus on, will this be an impactful experiment?
zh: 所以这本质上是不只关注，这将是一个有影响力的实验吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Think about what comes next and what comes next if this is true.
zh: 而是思考接下来是什么，如果这是真的，接下来又是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, I moved it.
zh: 好的，我把它挪动了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Particularly in a higher growth environment, you're not really looking for a 5% Statsig win.
zh: 特别是在高增长环境中，你不是真的在寻找 5% 的 Statsig 胜利。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're looking for something that totally moves the business and that has compounding effect over time.
zh: 你在寻找某种能彻底推动业务的东西，并且随着时间的推移有复合效应。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you just got to think through what that is.
zh: 所以你只需要想清楚那是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Something else you said that is changing in how PMs operate that you're very excited about is this move to IC work, PMs moving away from this kind of big org management world to actually doing the work.
zh: 你提到的另一件正在改变 PM 运作方式的事情，也是你非常兴奋的，就是这种向独立贡献者工作的转变，PM 从这种大组织管理世界转向真正做工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Talk about that and what that means for the role of product management.
zh: 谈谈那一点，以及它对产品管理角色意味着什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mentioned a little bit earlier, but there was this thing in the ratio land where what you did if you were really successful as a PM is you got promoted into being a director.
zh: 我早些时候提到过一点，但在 Ratio Land 曾有这样一件事，如果你作为一个 PM 真的非常成功，你要做的事就是被提升为总监。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then all of a sudden it was like, don't be hands-on anymore.
zh: 然后突然之间就像是这样，不要再动手了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your goal is just to coach and guide.
zh: 你的目标只是指导和引导。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we took all of our A players and then promoted them out of doing things.
zh: 所以我们把所有的 A 类球员提拔出来，让他们不再做具体事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they spent all of their time in alignment and they spent all of their time coaching and tweaking what their team was doing.
zh: 他们把所有时间花在协调上，把所有时间花在指导和微调他们的团队在做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you get this really yo-yo development process where somebody does all this work, it goes to review, it gets told no, and you're just going back and forward in reviews.
zh: 你会得到这种真正像溜溜球一样的开发过程，某人做了所有这些工作，拿去评审，被告知不行，你只是在评审中来来回回。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can see my scar tissue coming through.
zh: 你可以看到我的伤疤显露出来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: On our team, everybody is, there are managers, there's I think four or five people across the team who manage other PMs, all of them would spend 90 plus percent of their time doing IC work.
zh: 在我们的团队中，每个人都是，有管理者，我认为整个团队中有四五个人管理其他 PM，他们所有人会花 90% 以上的时间做 IC 工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm still probably 50% of my time doing IC work personally.
zh: 我个人可能仍然花 50% 的时间做 IC 工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think there's a couple real advantages of it.
zh: 我认为这有几个真正的优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first is if you are a kind of VP product where you've got a decade plus, maybe 15 years of experience building things, hopefully your instincts as to what's going to work and not are fairly well honed at this point.
zh: 第一个是，如果你是一种有十年以上，也许 15 年构建事物经验的 VP 产品，希望你对什么会行得通、什么行不通的直觉在此时已经被磨炼得相当好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can just make decisions more quickly than people.
zh: 你可以比人们更快地做出决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can have real impact very, very quickly.
zh: 你可以非常、非常快地产生真正的影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's really great for the organization to have somebody who can do that as opposed to the idea of working through three layers of we divide the problem up amongst a couple PMs.
zh: 组织里有这样的人真的很好，而不是那种我们要在三个层级中把问题分配给几个 PM 来解决的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those folks need to get into alignment.
zh: 那些人需要达成一致。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's different engineering teams debating stuff.
zh: 不同的工程团队在争论事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: You just tend to go.
zh: 你就直接行动。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's wonderful.
zh: 所以这很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the second thing is there's two ways that that ends up driving leverage.
zh: 我认为第二件事是这最终会驱动杠杆作用有两种方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is a VP in theory can handle the workload of multiple more junior PMs just because, as I said, they're more efficient.
zh: 一个是 VP 理论上可以处理多个初级 PM 的工作量，因为，正如我所说，他们更有效率。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that means that you see more of the board at any given point in time.
zh: 这意味着你在任何给定的时刻都能看到更多的棋盘。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you're far more likely to make the intuitively correct decision for how should we tune the discovery algorithm vis-a-vis people who ship slowly, which is an evergreen thing in e-comm.
zh: 所以你更有可能做出直觉上正确的决策，即我们应该如何调整发现算法相对于发货缓慢的人，这在电商中是一个长期存在的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, if you are thinking about how we manage sellers who ship slowly, and you know about the power of discovery, you can, in either case, make the correct decision.
zh: 嗯，如果你正在考虑我们如何管理发货缓慢的卖家，并且你了解发现的力量，那么在任何情况下，你都可以做出正确的决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the things that I remember plaguing Twitch for a long time, and I was probably one of the people more at fault of it than ever was discovery team and the ads team were always at war for impressions.
zh: 我记得困扰 Twitch 很久的一件事是，而且我可能是在这方面过错最大的人之一，就是发现团队和广告团队总是为了展示位而战。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where do ads go in the feed?
zh: 广告应该放在信息流的哪里？

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the impact to discovery metrics?
zh: 对发现指标有什么影响？

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the impact to ad dollars?
zh: 对广告收入有什么影响？

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the first things I did when I go up to Twitch was just put ads in discovery and make sure that there's the same PM who's accountable for both because they're going to make the natural trade-off that say the goal is GMV generated from the feed.
zh: 当我接手 Twitch 时做的第一件事就是把广告放在发现里，并确保有同一个 PM 对两者负责，因为他们会做出自然的权衡，即目标是信息流产生的 GMV。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of them is through organic.
zh: 其中之一是通过自然流量。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of them is through a paid substitution.
zh: 其中之一是通过付费替代。

speaker: Unknown
en: Solve.
zh: 解决它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you put the same person across multiple things, they tend to organically align those things and you just cut out months and months and months of back and forth and the politics that tends to take it from being company first to career first.
zh: 当你让同一个人负责多个事情时，他们往往会自然地使这些事情保持一致，你只需要削减几个月又几个月的来回扯皮，以及那些往往将事情从「公司优先」转变为「职业优先」的政治斗争。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so having VPs mostly in IC land, having directors mostly doing IC work, even having me having to grapple with IC work keeps everybody connected to the ground floor of what's actually true as opposed to what seems true in a review.
zh: 因此，让 VP 们主要待在 IC 领域，让总监们主要做 IC 工作，甚至让我不得不亲自处理 IC 工作，让每个人都保持与实际真实的底层相连，而不是在评审中看起来看似真实。

speaker: Unknown
en: But also means that you're more likely to make the intuitively correct decision early just because why wouldn't you want Messi playing for your team rather than trying to have the academy coming along all the time?
zh: 但这也意味着你更有可能在早期就做出直觉上正确的决策，仅仅是因为你为什么不希望梅西为你的球队效力，而不是试图一直让学院派跟上呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: I love this.
zh: 我喜欢这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when you talk about IC work for PM, what does IC work for PM in this context mean?
zh: 那么当你谈到 PM 的 IC 工作时，在这个语境下 PM 的 IC 工作意味着什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Does it mean shipping code building or is it like running a team, owning a roadmap, writing the strategy doc?
zh: 它是指编写代码构建，还是像管理团队、拥有路线图、撰写战略文档？

speaker: Unknown
en: Imagine it's the second bucket.
zh: 想象它是第二类。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whatever is required to most effectively ship is the short answer.
zh: 无论什么是最有效交付所需的，这就是简短的回答。

speaker: Unknown
en: Have I personally shipped some production code at Whatnot?
zh: 我个人在 Whatnot 上写过一些生产代码吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do I think that's really the best use of my time?
zh: 我认为那真的是我时间的最佳利用方式吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Not really.
zh: 不完全是。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm certain that quietly somebody reworked most of my code in order to ensure that the linting was correct and the localization worked and all of the nuance that decades of software engineering has taught you that me and Claude Code did not get right.
zh: 我确信有人悄悄地重写了我的大部分代码，以确保 Linting 是正确的，本地化是有效的，以及几十年的软件工程教给你的所有细微之处，而我和 Claude Code 并没有做对。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I do think it starts with, are you literally in the support tickets?
zh: 但我认为这首先始于，你真的在支持工单中吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you know what customer problems we're having?
zh: 你知道我们正在遇到什么客户问题吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Have you pulled all of the data yourself so that you actually understand it?
zh: 你自己拉取了所有数据以便你真正理解它吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Have you sat with engineering and design?
zh: 你和工程与设计坐在一起吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Have you queried the code base directly in order to understand how things work?
zh: 你为了理解事情如何运作而直接查询了代码库吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then have you written the spec?
zh: 然后你写了规格说明吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you then running, you stand up, and we go?
zh: 然后你在负责运作吗，你站起来，我们就出发？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think all of that is just core individual IC work.
zh: 我认为所有这些只是核心的个人 IC 工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of people that have worked their way up the ladder of product, become a VP, and it doesn't feel exciting to go back to being an IC.
zh: 有很多人在产品阶梯上一步步爬上去，成为了 VP，而回去做 IC 并不令人兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some people, clearly you love it, you enjoy it.
zh: 有些人，显然你喜欢它，你享受它。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of people are like, oh, I thought I was done with this.
zh: 很多人就像，噢，我以为我已经做完这个了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I could just work through people.
zh: 我可以通过别人来工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I could think big picture.
zh: 我可以思考大局。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you feel about that?
zh: 你对此感觉如何？

speaker: Unknown
en: What would you say to folks in that bucket?
zh: 你会对那一类人说什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there are probably still a load of organizations where that is really valuable and that they will go.
zh: 我认为可能仍然有很多组织，那里这真的很有价值，而且他们会去那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: My recruiting tends to be the folks who are, oh my God, I used to love product management and I'm so sick of sitting in alignment meetings.
zh: 我的招聘倾向于那些人是，噢天哪，我曾经热爱产品管理，而且我受够了坐在对齐会议上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm out there pitching CPOs and VPs of product to be like, "Don't you miss actually doing things?
zh: 我在外面向 CPO 和产品 VP 推销，就像说，「难道你不怀念真正做事情吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you want to come back?"
zh: 你想回来吗？」

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's okay for us to acknowledge that there'll be a bifurcation across the industry.
zh: 我认为我们可以承认业界将会出现分化，这没关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: I do think that there are organizations that are sufficiently large that maybe everyone being hands-on isn't right.
zh: 我确实认为有些组织足够大，以至于每个人都亲力亲为可能是不对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I also think I mentioned earlier that you have to have a matching culture to go with this kind of environment where that's the expectation.
zh: 我也认为我之前提到过，你必须有一种匹配的文化来伴随这种环境，这是期望所在。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where people are like, "I don't want to talk about it.
zh: 在那里人们就像，「我不想谈论它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to just, let's go and do that thing."
zh: 我只想，让我们去做那件事吧。」

speaker: Unknown
en: And in a lot of ways, every startup is a reflection of their founders.
zh: 在很多方面，每个初创公司都是其创始人的反映。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that naturally tends to be how do they think and how do they want to run the organization?
zh: 所以这自然往往是他们如何思考以及他们如何想要运营组织的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I've actually found that, for a lot of the cases, you go and talk to somebody who spent the last five, six years as a senior director at Meta who spends their entire time in alignment meetings, and they miss actually talking to customers and talking to engineers and shipping things.
zh: 但实际上我发现，在很多情况下，你去和一个在 Meta 担任了五六年的高级总监交谈，他们把所有时间都花在对齐会议上，他们怀念真正与客户交谈、与工程师交谈和交付东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: What makes me think about it, I imagine you've seen this list of all of these chief technology officers that have gone to become just engineers at Anthropic.
zh: 让我想到这一点的是，我想你应该见过这个名单，上面有所有这些首席技术官都跑去 Anthropic 当普通工程师了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I pulled up this list as you were talking.
zh: 你说话的时候我就调出了这个名单。

speaker: Unknown
en: The CTO of Workday is just a member of technical staff at Anthropic.
zh: Workday 的 CTO 现在只是 Anthropic 的一名普通技术人员。

speaker: Unknown
en: CTO of Instagram, Box's CTO, Super.com's CTO.
zh: Instagram 的 CTO，Box 的 CTO，Super.com 的 CTO。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're just like engineers now at Anthropic.
zh: 他们现在在 Anthropic 就是工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yep.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is my greatest desire that the Whatnot product bench basically looks like that.
zh: 我最大的愿望是，Whatnot 的产品基准基本上看起来就是那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of these people with great skills and great understanding and actually end up coming and building as ICs.
zh: 所有这些拥有高超技能和深刻理解的人，最终能以 IC 的身份加入并进行构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: What about the comp of this path?
zh: 这条路径的薪酬怎么样？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's people's dream, move up to VP, make millions of dollars.
zh: 人们的梦想是升到 VP，赚几百万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there a world where you can still do that and be an IC?
zh: 有没有一个世界，你仍然可以做这些并且是个 IC？

speaker: Unknown
en: I actually think it's easier.
zh: 我其实觉得这更容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: Spicy take.
zh: 这观点很大胆。

speaker: Unknown
en: But go and take the comp required to have five L5s reporting to one L7 and then four L7s reporting to one VP, and now total the comp of that product org and turn around and say, "What if I had three people?
zh: 去算算这种配置所需的薪酬，五个 L5 汇报给一个 L7，然后四个 L7 汇报给一个 VP，然后总计那个产品组织的薪酬，转身说，“如果我只有三个人呢？”

speaker: Unknown
en: Why can't I pay them all D2 VP money, particularly if they're having the level of impact that those folks are having there?
zh: 我为什么不给他们都付 D2 VP 的钱，特别是如果他们产生的影响跟那群人在那儿产生的影响一样大呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: Why not?"
zh: 为什么不呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: And just to fully understand why this is happening and why this should happen, what I'm hearing, there's kind of many combinations.
zh: 为了完全理解为什么这正在发生以及为什么这应该发生，我听到的是，这有很多种组合。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is AI is enabling this, which is great.
zh: 一个是 AI 正在促成这一点，这很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: Perfect timing.
zh: 时机完美。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the other motivations to do this?
zh: 这样做的其他动机是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it just the product ends up being better?
zh: 只是产品最终变得更好了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it fewer people?
zh: 是因为人更少了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I certainly think the product ends up being better.
zh: 我当然认为产品最终会变得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the things that folks have been telling us for a long time is, yeah, that won't scale.
zh: 人们很久以来一直告诉我们的一件事是，是的，那无法规模化。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, leadership isn't going to be able to stay hands-on with what's going on.
zh: 哦，领导层将无法保持对正在发生的事情的亲力亲为。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're going to need to go and hire tons more layers.
zh: 你需要去聘请更多的层级。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what we found is that's actually not true.
zh: 而我们发现那其实不是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It requires a different muscle.
zh: 这需要一种不同的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to make an effort to make sure you genuinely understand ground truth.
zh: 你必须做出努力，确保你真正了解基本事实。

speaker: Unknown
en: An example we use all the time is we'll be talking in a growth meeting and someone will say, "Oh yeah, but that was fraud."
zh: 我们一直用的一个例子是，我们在一个增长会议上，有人会说，“哦是的，但那是欺诈。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Turn around and be like, "How do you know that was fraud?"
zh: 然后转身说，“你怎么知道那是欺诈？”

speaker: Unknown
en: "Oh, it's labeled in the dataset as fraud.
zh: “哦，它在数据集里被标记为欺诈。”

speaker: Unknown
en: "Okay.
zh: “好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you know how it gets labeled?"
zh: 你知道它是怎么被标记的吗？”

speaker: Unknown
en: "I assume someone in ops does it."
zh: “我假设是运营部门的某个人做的。”

speaker: Unknown
en: "Okay, do you know the SOP or how they label that?"
zh: “好的，你知道 SOP 或者他们怎么标记那个吗？”

speaker: Unknown
en: "No."
zh: “不知道。”

speaker: Unknown
en: "Okay, so you don't know it's fraud."
zh: “好的，所以你不知道那是欺诈。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you push a really experienced product director like that, they're going to go, "Good point, I don't.
zh: 如果你这样逼问一位真正经验丰富的产品总监，他们会说，“说得好，我确实不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to go find out."
zh: 我去弄清楚。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you invariably end up strengthening the system that agents are using to data label because suddenly there's a very smart person who's very invested in understanding how we do that and helping guide it.
zh: 然后你最终会不可避免地加强智能体用来做数据标记的系统，因为突然有了一个非常聪明的人，非常投入于了解我们如何做这件事并帮助指导它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so just that attitude that says we're going to do fewer things, we're going to make sure we execute the hell out of them, and we're going to push our best people to be in the weeds everywhere means that you fix lots of things as you go and you don't end up just making loads of trade-offs.
zh: 所以那种我们要做更少事情的态度，我们要确保我们完美地执行它们，我们要推动我们最好的人深入到每个细节，这意味着你在进行过程中修复了很多事情，你最终不会做出大量的权衡。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think there's a general belief that it's too easy otherwise for growth to hide all sins.
zh: 我认为有一种普遍的看法是，否则增长太容易掩盖所有问题了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You get bigger and you just end up scaling and everybody's working off of averages.
zh: 你变得更大，你最终只是规模化，每个人都基于平均水平工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So culturally, I think you've got to be really committed to let's whole ass a few things, as I tend to say sometimes.
zh: 所以在文化上，我认为你必须真正致力于全力以赴地做几件事，就像我有时会说的一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Shout out Ron Swanson.
zh: 致敬 Ron Swanson。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then push your best people to be really in the weeds of stuff.
zh: 然后推动你们最好的人真正深入到事情的一线细节中去。

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually what you find over time is you end up being more efficient by doing that because you actually understand how things work the first time and you make the best decisions.
zh: 实际上随着时间的推移你会发现，那样做效率更高，因为你实际上第一次就明白了事情是如何运作的，并且你做出了最好的决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then listen, AI, huge leverage for all of this.
zh: 然后听着，AI，对这一切都是巨大的杠杆。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can't think of how much time I spent as a junior PM asking my engineers how hard something would be, and distracting actual velocity in order to help scope future stuff.
zh: 我想象不出我作为初级 PM 时花了多少时间问工程师做某件事有多难，为了帮助规划未来的事情而分散了实际的速度。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now I can sit and talk to Claude and understand roughly LOEs.
zh: 现在我可以坐下来和 Claude 交谈，并大致理解 LOEs。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can sit there and go through and be like, it feels like there's some car crash of modals that must be hitting new users as they open up the app.
zh: 我可以坐在那里，浏览一遍，然后感觉就像，看起来有一些 modals 的严重冲突，肯定会在新用户打开应用时冲击他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can literally just go through and be like, let's load up the feed and talk to me about the logic of who sees what in what order and when does this thing fire?
zh: 你真的可以就这样浏览一遍，然后说，让我们加载一下 feed，然后跟我讲讲谁在什么顺序下看到什么以及这东西什么时候触发的逻辑？

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can get answers really quickly.
zh: 而且你可以非常快地得到答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: And having, as I said before, folks with enough tenure and enough reps that they can see that and say, "You know what?
zh: 而且，正如我之前所说，拥有那些资历足够深、经验足够丰富的人，他们可以看到这一点并说，“你知道吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's bad.
zh: 那很糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's just make a good decision and change the ordering of those."
zh: 让我们做一个好的决定，改变这些的顺序。”

speaker: Unknown
en: I've saved now a kickoff meeting, an alignment meeting, a week writing PRDs, experiment time, all of that by just having somebody who's kind of empowered to go and make a decision.
zh: 我现在节省了一个启动会议、一个对齐会议、一周写 PRD 的时间、实验时间，所有这些都是因为拥有一个被授权去做决定的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So coming back to people that are trying to get a job as a PM, whether you're new, let's actually hold off on new people, but people that are say managers, senior folks that are just like, wow, the market has really shifted.
zh: 所以回到那些试图找 PM 工作的人，无论你是新手，让我们实际上先搁置新人，但是那些比如说经理、资深人士，只是觉得，哇，市场真的变了。

speaker: Unknown
en: A big thing we're hearing right now is you need to be comfortable with moving back into IC, giving up your fancy title.
zh: 我们现在听到的一件大事是，你需要对回到 IC 工作、放弃你花哨的头衔感到适应。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there anything more along those lines of just people looking for a job, struggling to find a job?
zh: 对于那些找工作、挣扎着找工作的人来说，还有更多这方面的建议吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Any other advice for them?
zh: 给他们的其他建议吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Start doing IC work in the role you're in would be my push.
zh: 在你现在的角色中开始做 IC 工作将是我的建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: Get back to the basics of make sure that you're taking on practical work.
zh: 回到基础，确保你正在承担实际的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because I just think it's good to make sure that you are keeping those muscles well honed.
zh: 因为我只是认为，确保你保持那些肌肉磨练得很好是很好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it also starts with pushing internally for those things.
zh: 我认为这也始于在内部推动这些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would bet that if you started bringing that level of productivity back into the role that you're in, it probably helps you where you are in addition to help you where you might move to.
zh: 我敢打赌，如果你开始把那种生产力水平带回你现在的角色，它可能会帮助你在你所在的地方，也有助于你可能会搬到的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think there's a lot of chatter online obviously about PMs or engineers now.
zh: 但我认为，显然在网上有很多关于 PM 或工程师的闲聊。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's all well and good.
zh: 我认为那都是很好很好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a great muscle to go and go and hone.
zh: 这是一个很好的肌肉可以去磨练。

speaker: Unknown
en: As I said, I've pushed some production code because I wanted to go through the exercise of understanding it.
zh: 正如我所说，我推送了一些生产代码，因为我想通过这个练习来理解它。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think there's also, before you get to building things, it's like how quickly can you get back into the muscle of scoping the correct thing, understanding the problem, being able to define what good looks like?
zh: 但我认为还有，在开始构建东西之前，就像你能多快回到界定正确的事情、理解问题、能够定义什么是好的样子的肌肉中？

speaker: Unknown
en: And take advantage of the scale and the scope that you've got that you can see more and bring more to things.
zh: 并利用你拥有的规模和范围，你可以看到更多，并为事情带来更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think most folks who've sat in a director plus role will know the pain of sitting there and watching a junior PM yo-yo back and forth on the same PRD back to review where you kind of know what the answer is.
zh: 我想大多数担任过总监及以上角色的人都知道坐在那里的痛苦，看着一个初级 PM 在同一个 PRD 上反复来回，回到审查，而你基本上知道答案是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Somewhere along the way we decided that lead a horse to water as opposed to help them understand the answer and then keep moving.
zh: 在这个过程中的某个地方，我们决定了把马牵到水边，而不是帮助他们理解答案，然后继续前进。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think there's something in our coaching styles that we can get back to of help somebody understand what good looks like relatively quickly as opposed to just endless review yo-yo.
zh: 我认为我们的辅导风格中有一些东西可以回归到帮助某人相对快速地理解什么是好的样子，而不是无休止的审查来回拉锯。

speaker: Unknown
en: This point you make about PMs not shipping to production, I so agree with.
zh: 你提出的关于 PM 不发货到生产的观点，我非常赞同。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because my mind changed on this recently with a previous podcast guest with this point that PMs have so much more leverage if they're not sitting there trying to ship to production.
zh: 因为我的观点最近改变了，这是与之前的一位播客嘉宾就这一点交流后，即 PM 如果不是坐在那里试图发货到生产，他们有更多的杠杆作用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Enabling the team to ship better and faster and making sure the things that are shipping are better is a much better use of PM's time than sitting there shipping stuff.
zh: 赋能团队更好更快地发货，并确保发货的东西更好，这是 PM 时间的更好的利用方式，而不是坐在那里发货东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, this sounds really silly, mate, but it takes me substantially longer to go through the minutia of getting, get, commit, and all of the pieces that are second eng to engineer aligned than it does to actually work out what the problem is and be able to describe it.
zh: 我的意思是，这听起来真的很傻，伙计，但我花了更长的时间去浏览 getting、get、commit 的细枝末节以及所有工程师与工程师对齐的片段，而不是去实际弄清问题是什么并能够描述它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So yes, good practice to try and make sure you're doing something.
zh: 所以是的，试着确保你正在做一些事情的好习惯。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, I don't want to judge if our dev tools have gotten easier or not based on what someone tells me.
zh: 例如，我不想根据某人告诉我的内容来判断我们的开发工具是否变得更容易了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to go and try it and be like, yep, that was easier than last time I did it.
zh: 我要去尝试一下，然后说，是的，这比我上次做的时候更容易了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I do think you can get an awful long way understanding the code base and then talking to somebody who can actually execute well.
zh: 但我确实认为你可以通过理解代码库然后与一个真正能执行好的人交谈来走很远。

speaker: Unknown
en: Otherwise you're just going to get fall afoul of a thousand classic traps that every other engineer learned how not to do when they were an L4.
zh: 否则你将陷入一千个经典的陷阱，而这些陷阱是其他每个工程师在还是 L4 的时候就学会了如何避免的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So following that thread a little bit, what are some of the ways that AI has enabled you and/or your team to move faster and be more productive other than prototyping, which is the very clear benefit of AI for PMs and product teams?
zh: 所以顺着这个话题稍微深入一点，AI 有哪些方式让你和/或你的团队移动得更快、更有效率，除了原型制作，这显然是 AI 对 PM 和产品团队的明显好处？

speaker: Unknown
en: What else?
zh: 还有呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are maybe in the top three of, wow, this has really unlocked our productivity and the quality of what we do?
zh: 也许在前三名中是什么，哇，这真的解锁了我们的生产力和我们所做事情的质量？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, the first one I think by a country mile is data science.
zh: 我的意思是，我认为第一个遥遥领先的是数据科学。

speaker: Unknown
en: We use Hex threads internally at Whatnot.
zh: 我们在 Whatnot 内部使用 Hex threads。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm sure there are other comparable products, but I think it's almost hard to remember time as a PM before you had tooling like that where you could genuinely start pulling very nuanced cohorts of data where you could grab an individual user where you've heard a report.
zh: 我敢肯定有其他类似的产品，但我认为几乎很难记得在拥有像这样的工具之前的 PM 时光，在那里你可以真正开始提取非常细致的数据队列，你可以抓取一个你听到报告的个别用户。

speaker: Unknown
en: Actually understand, let's pull logs, help me understand exactly what this user did and saw.
zh: 实际上理解，让我们拉取日志，帮我准确理解这个用户做了什么和看到了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: How many other users look like this?
zh: 有多少其他用户看起来像这样？

speaker: Unknown
en: What would impact be?
zh: 影响会是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then all of a sudden you can build pretty meaningful sensitivity models or forecasts of what might happen, regression models, et cetera, really, really, really quickly, which is incredibly powerful.
zh: 然后突然之间你可以构建非常有意义的敏感性模型或预测可能会发生什么的模型、回归模型等等，非常非常非常快，这是非常强大的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other thing that we've found is it helps us move much more quickly with shipping things because you can spot regressions and weird knock-on effects of two products into mixing more quickly than you used to be able to.
zh: 我们发现的另一件事是，它帮助我们在发货东西方面移动得更快，因为你可以比以前更快地发现两个产品混合产生的回归和奇怪的连锁效应。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think in really large complicated systems, that's always one of the things that ends up slowing you down of release trends and all of that versus if you build the right AI tool, you can spot regressions really quickly, which basically lets people just go.
zh: 我认为在真正的大型复杂系统中，这总是最终拖慢你的事情之一，发布趋势等等，如果你构建正确的 AI 工具，你可以非常快地发现回归，这基本上让人们直接行动。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I don't know what the future of data science looks like.
zh: 所以我不知道数据科学的未来看起来是什么样。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think as a product manager, I've spent less time in the last year talking to a data scientist than I ever have in my career, even though I've probably spent 10 times more time in data and understanding actually how the product's working than I ever have in my career.
zh: 但我认为作为一个产品经理，我在过去一年里花在与数据科学家交谈的时间比我职业生涯中任何时候都少，即使我可能花在数据和实际理解产品如何工作上的时间比我在职业生涯中任何时候都多 10 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that one I think is really powerful.
zh: 所以我认为那一点真的很强大。

speaker: Unknown
en: Second one I've already mentioned, which is stop bothering engineers with how does the code base work?
zh: 第二个我已经提到了，那就是别再去烦工程师们问代码库是怎么工作的了？

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually just go and talk to Claude and understand it, which is really helpful.
zh: 实际上直接去跟 Claude 谈并理解它，这真的很有帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: I used to say early on in my career that the goal was always to be understand your systems at the boxes and lines level of which system drives which thing.
zh: 我职业生涯早期常说，目标总是要在框框和线条的层面理解你的系统，即哪个系统驱动哪个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now there's no excuse not to understand that or a nuanced layer.
zh: 而现在没有借口不去理解那个层面或更细致的层面了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the other one, and this might be very specific to Whatnot, so I don't know that this will help everyone, but one of the things that I've been lucky to do in my career is basically worked on live products for a decade now.
zh: 但另一点，这一点可能非常针对 Whatnot，所以我不知道这是否对每个人都有帮助，但我职业生涯中一直很幸运做的一件事基本上就是在现在的产品上工作了十年。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's always been really cool to be able to ship a product and then watch a customer use it and watch them figure it out.
zh: 所以能够发布产品然后看着客户使用它并看着他们弄明白它，一直都很酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think people have just gotten this experience with Listen Labs and others in that cohort of watching people use your product.
zh: 我认为人们通过 Listen Labs 和那个队列里的其他人已经获得了这种观看人们使用你的产品的体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I've always been able to sit and watch people use a thing for the first time and go through that new user comprehension gap.
zh: 我一直能够坐下来看着人们第一次使用一个东西，并经历那个新用户理解鸿沟。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's really cool with a bunch of the AI tooling right now is as they're describing, oh, I'm having a problem, you can literally be watching the code base live and work out, is that actually a bug that's happening right now right now?
zh: 现在一堆 AI 工具真正酷的地方在于，当他们描述“哦，我遇到了一个问题”时，你可以实时地观看代码库并弄清楚，这真的是现在正在发生的 Bug 吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or is that a comprehension gap where it doesn't work as expected?
zh: 还是这是一个理解鸿沟，即它没有按预期工作？

speaker: Unknown
en: And suddenly you've got this video artifact of someone using your product, you can be analyzing the code base in real time, and you can be just talking through AI to the code base to understand what's actually happening.
zh: 突然间你有了某人使用你产品的视频产物，你可以实时分析代码库，你可以通过 AI 对着代码库说话来理解实际发生了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's like a feedback loop on steroids because all of a sudden you know exactly what's going on, customer side, code side, and observe side as a viewer in real time, which is really cool.
zh: 这就像一个超级强力的反馈循环，因为突然间你确切地知道发生了什么，客户端、代码端和观察端，作为实时观看者，这真的很酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: That sounds both awesome and very stressful to be building products that are that live in real time.
zh: 这听起来既很棒又压力很大，要构建那种实时实时的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think about Netflix where they invest in Live Now, and that's just all you've done for 10 years and how big a deal that was for them.
zh: 我想到了 Netflix，他们投资了 Live Now，而这正是你 10 年来一直在做的所有事情，这对他们来说是多么重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know the scale is different.
zh: 我知道规模是不同的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Honestly, my second week at Whatnot, I remember sitting in a room watching, so one of those not familiar kind of commerce, largely auction platform, live commerce platform.
zh: 老实说，我在 Whatnot 的第二周，我记得坐在一个房间里看着，所以那些不熟悉某种类型商业的人，主要是拍卖平台，实时商业平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's varieties of different ways to run an auction, but one of them is what's called sudden death, which is like when the timer ends, it ends.
zh: 拍卖有不同的运行方式，但其中一种叫做突然死亡法，就像计时器结束时，它就结束了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Otherwise, the classic auction environment, somebody bids in the last five seconds, it adds 10 seconds back on the clock, and a seller can decide what auction model they want.
zh: 否则，在经典的拍卖环境中，有人在最后五秒出价，它会在时钟上加回 10 秒，卖家可以决定他们想要什么拍卖模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was sitting there watching a seller who was like, "These are taking too long.
zh: 我坐在那里看着一个卖家，他说，“这些时间太长了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wish this seven-second timer was actually three seconds because I want to move more product."
zh: 我希望这个七秒的计时器实际上是三秒，因为我想卖出更多产品。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And I watched two engineers in the office look at each other, and be like, "That's a [inaudible 00:39:33].
zh: 我看着办公室里的两个工程师看着对方，说，“那是个 [听不清 00:39:33]。

speaker: Unknown
en: We could totally do that."
zh: 我们完全可以做到。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And so they went and updated it in real time and then jumped in the chat of a show, and just said, "Refresh your app."
zh: 所以他们实时去更新了它，然后跳进一个节目的聊天中，只是说，“刷新你的应用。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And then all of a sudden, bang, it was operating that way.
zh: 突然间，砰，它就开始那样运作了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was like, "Cool.
zh: 我就像，“酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm with my people.
zh: 我跟我的同伴在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm in the right place."
zh: 我来对地方了。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Because that's the level of responsiveness that you can get in a live environment.
zh: 因为这就是你在实时环境中可以获得的那种响应级别。

speaker: Unknown
en: And obviously AI means that that's really easy for lots of people to take on.
zh: 显然 AI 意味着这对很多人来说都很容易上手。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not that I would touch production code in that kind of way because that's a disastrous idea.
zh: 并不是说我会以那种方式接触生产代码，因为那是一个灾难性的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: But for qualified humans, it's a wonderful one.
zh: 但对于合格的人类来说，这是一个绝妙的主意。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is very cool.
zh: 那非常酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: This episode is brought to you by Mercury, radically different banking loved by over 300,000 entrepreneurs, and now with Command.
zh: 本集由 Mercury 赞助，这是一种截然不同的银行业务，受到超过 30 万名创业者的喜爱，现在还有了 Command。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've been a customer of Mercury's for over six years.
zh: 我做 Mercury 的客户已经六年多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have never once though about leaving.
zh: 我从未想过要离开。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mercury is basically what happens when banking is built by product people, not by bankers.
zh: Mercury 基本上就是当银行业务是由产品人员而不是银行家构建时会发生的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: They make it so easy, dare I say fun, to send invoices, move money around, set up virtual cards for folks on my team.
zh: 它们让发送发票、转移资金、为我的团队成员设置虚拟卡片变得如此简单，我敢说很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: Does your bank have an API, a terminal native CLI, or an AI-ready MCP server?
zh: 你的银行有 API、终端原生 CLI 或 AI 就绪的 MCP 服务器吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think so.
zh: 我不这么认为。

speaker: Unknown
en: And just recently they launched Command, a conversational interface built directly into Mercury, which acts as your financial operator.
zh: 就在最近他们推出了 Command，一个直接构建到 Mercury 中的对话界面，充当你的财务操作员。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've been using Command to transfer money around, to figure out what categories I've been spending the most money in, analyze my cash flows.
zh: 我一直在使用 Command 来转移资金，弄清楚我在哪些类别上花钱最多，分析我的现金流。

speaker: Unknown
en: And just today, I used it to find out how much I've made from a specific sponsor over the past year.
zh: 就在今天，我用它来找出我过去一年从某个赞助商那里赚了多少钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just ask, how much have I made from X over the past year?
zh: 我只是问，我过去一年从 X 那里赚了多少钱？

speaker: Unknown
en: 10 seconds later, I have an answer.
zh: 10 秒后，我得到了答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is so freaking cool.
zh: 这真的太酷了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Visit mercury.com to learn more and apply online in minutes.
zh: 访问 mercury.com 了解更多信息并在几分钟内在线申请。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mercury is a FinTech company, not an FDIC insured bank.
zh: Mercury 是一家金融科技公司，不是 FDIC 承保的银行。

speaker: Unknown
en: Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group in column NA members FDIC.
zh: 银行业务由 Choice Financial Group 和 column NA 提供，成员 FDIC。

speaker: Unknown
en: Coming back to this data science point, I have a friend who's a data scientist, and he said it's a rough time for data scientists because of this exact thing.
zh: 回到这个数据科学观点，我有一个朋友是数据科学家，他说由于这个确切的原因，现在是数据科学家的艰难时期。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to add a little more color, basically their time used to be asked to do some data analysis, do some work with the data, come back, here's the results, I'm confident in this conclusion.
zh: 为了多补充一点细节，基本上他们的时间过去被要求做一些数据分析，用数据做一些工作，回来，这里是结果，我对这个结论有信心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now their time is basically seeing half-assed data science work from non-data scientists, and just show me, is this right?
zh: 现在他们的时间基本上是看那些非数据科学家做的半吊子数据科学工作，然后就是给我看，这对吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then half the time it's wrong.
zh: 然后有一半的时间都是错的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're like, "What the hell is my job now?
zh: 然后他们会说，“我现在的工作到底是鬼样子？

speaker: Unknown
en: It sucks."
zh: 这太糟了。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, listen, I have a lot of empathy for that because I've certainly seen it.
zh: 是的，听着，我对此很有同理心，因为我肯定见过这种情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: Another plug for why having fewer more senior PMs is helpful because those are folks who've seen more of those reps and understand.
zh: 再插一句，为什么拥有更少但更资深的 PM 会有帮助，因为那些人见过更多这种迭代，并且理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I also think a lot of the time that lack of clarity comes from the other thing, which is organizations historically underinvested in data engineering and data structures and good data labeling, and whether or not you've got, not just your taxonomies right, but whether or not you really understand whether or not your data systems and structures are set up well.
zh: 但我也认为很多时候这种清晰度的缺失来自另一件事，那就是组织历史上在数据工程、数据结构和良好的数据标注方面投入不足，以及你是否不仅把你的分类体系搞对了，而且你是否真正理解你的数据系统和结构是否设置得当。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what we've found is a lot of our best data scientists are pushing in that direction of are we actually correctly updating all of the ways in which our tracking and attribution works so that it's less easy for people to misunderstand those?
zh: 所以我们发现，我们许多最好的数据科学家正朝着这个方向努力，我们要真正正确地更新我们跟踪和归因工作的所有方式，这样人们就不容易误解这些东西？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then yeah, using an AI tool to find a piece of data, much like using an AI tool to write code, doesn't absolve you of responsibility to make sure that that was good analysis, good code.
zh: 然后是的，使用 AI 工具查找一条数据，就像使用 AI 工具写代码一样，并不能免除你确保那是良好分析、良好代码的责任。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just tends to be leveraged for those people who are naturally inclined that way.
zh: 它往往只是被那些天生倾向于这种方式的人所利用。

speaker: Unknown
en: So thinking about these different functions, data science, user research, design, engineering, PM, what I'm hearing so far is we'll need probably fewer PMs, we'll need fewer data scientists.
zh: 所以考虑这些不同的职能，数据科学、用户研究、设计、工程、PM，我目前听到的是，我们可能需要更少的 PM，我们需要更少的数据科学家。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are there any other roles that you think they're trending down in terms of we'll need... Are there any roles trending up like, wow, we're going to need a lot more of this kind of person?
zh: 你觉得还有其他角色正在呈下降趋势吗，关于我们需要……有哪些角色呈上升趋势吗，比如，哇，我们需要更多这类人？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, funnily enough, as I say, I haven't spoken to a data scientist in a while.
zh: 嗯，有趣的是，正如我所说，我有一阵子没跟数据科学家说话了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've certainly still hired plenty because I do think all that tracking and attribution and measurement, really, really powerful.
zh: 我们当然仍然雇佣了很多，因为我确实认为所有那些跟踪和归因以及衡量，真的、非常强大。

speaker: Unknown
en: I also think one of the flip sides, if we say we need fewer, it's like fewer of for the same output doesn't necessarily mean fewer of in macro.
zh: 我也认为另一面，如果我们说我们需要更少，这就像是对于相同产出而言的更少，并不一定意味着宏观上的更少。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because if you are using these systems right, you can just grow more quickly.
zh: 因为如果你正确使用这些系统，你可以只是增长得更快。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can build more things, you can take on more stuff.
zh: 你可以构建更多的东西，你可以承担更多的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I would be surprised actually if we ended up with net fewer.
zh: 所以如果我们最终在净数量上更少，我会感到惊讶。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's more like net fewer vis-a-vis customer impact for both.
zh: 我认为这更像是对于两者来说，相对于客户影响的净更少。

speaker: Unknown
en: Certainly I think trending up over time within these roles are these kind of, and I don't remember the exact label that people used to use, but this idea of tech leads that are kind of like a hybrid EM where you're running a very small team, running at things.
zh: 当然，我认为在这些角色中随时间推移呈上升趋势的是这类，我不记得人们以前使用的确切标签，但是这种技术负责人的想法，有点像混合型的 EM，你正在管理一个非常小的团队，处理事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because same way that we'd say the cost of trying something has come down, the idea that says you can have core focus, which is a thing we're very big on.
zh: 因为就像我们说尝试某事的成本已经下降一样，你拥有核心关注点（这是我们非常看重的一件事）这个想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've also found incubating a lot of smaller teams to go over and sit in the corner and just try and build this thing.
zh: 我们还发现孵化许多更小的团队去角落坐着，只是尝试构建这个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not quite prototyping, but it's like go and take a swing at a thing that we've historically thought was too hard, is getting cheaper and increasingly has very high leverage.
zh: 这不完全是在制作原型，但就像去尝试一个我们历史上认为太难的事情，正变得更便宜，并且 increasingly 具有非常高的杠杆作用。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the idea of engineering manager light, for want of a better term, is the thing that I'm definitely think that we'll see more and more of.
zh: 所以这个工程经理轻量级的想法，权且这么叫，是我绝对认为我们会越来越多看到的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not quite the technical member of staff, although that must be lovely, but certainly not the kind of full-blown EM role I think is one that definitely will come about more often.
zh: 这不太像是技术成员（尽管那一定很棒），但也肯定不是那种全面的 EM 角色，我认为这是一个肯定会更经常出现的角色。

speaker: Unknown
en: So maybe just to close the loop on this part of the conversation, there's this trend towards everyone's kind of a builder, PMs are shipping a little bit, being a little more engineer.
zh: 所以也许只是为了结束这一部分的对话，有一种趋势，每个人都是某种构建者，PM 正在稍微发布一些东西，更像一点工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: Engineers are taking on more of the PM work.
zh: 工程师正在承担更多的 PM 工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you think this just maybe plays out over the next couple of years in terms of what product teams look like broadly?
zh: 你认为这在未来几年会如何发展，就广泛的产品团队而言？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it still PM engineers, a designer, data scientist somewhere?
zh: 仍然是 PM、工程师、设计师、数据科学家在某个地方吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you envision the canonical product team over the coming years?
zh: 你如何设想未来几年的典型产品团队？

speaker: Unknown
en: Great question.
zh: 好问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I don't know that I know what it looks like everywhere.
zh: 我不知道我在每个地方都知道它是什么样子的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think what it'll look like at Whatnot is it probably still looks mostly like it has historically, which is there are reasons that you would have a specialist designer, specialist engineers, specialist product management.
zh: 我认为在 Whatnot 它看起来可能大部分像历史上一样，也就是有理由拥有专门的设计师、专门的工程师、专门的产品管理。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think those very concrete teams will largely be preserved for very specific projects or things that we have high confidence or conviction that we need to solve, or we're pretty high confidence conviction that we have a path forward on a thing and we want to make good progress.
zh: 我认为那些非常具体的团队将主要被保留用于非常具体的项目或我们有很高信心或信念我们需要解决的事情，或者我们非常有信心/信念我们在某件事上有前进的道路，并且我们希望取得良好进展。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think at the edges around that, there's going to be a lot more free space for people to play on like, "Hey, I'm reasonably sure I can go and make a meaningful improvement to this thing."
zh: 我认为在那周围的边缘，将会有更多的自由空间让人们去发挥，比如，“嘿，我有相当把握我可以去对这个东西做有意义的改进。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And it doesn't matter if you are a designer, an engineer, a product manager, a data scientist, you can and you should.
zh: 无论你是设计师、工程师、产品经理还是数据科学家，都不重要，你可以而且你应该。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're sitting there on a Friday afternoon and you can't focus on the POD you're writing, but you're pretty sure you can go and fix something, go for it.
zh: 如果你在周五下午坐在那里，无法专注于你正在写的 POD，但你相当确定你可以去修复某个东西，那就去吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think it probably doesn't morph in the more formal sense, but I do think there's just a lot more free space for people who are well-versed in the customer problems, well-versed in the code base, and understand some of that macro context.
zh: 所以我认为它可能不会在更正式的意义上发生形态变化，但我确实认为对于那些精通客户问题、精通代码库并理解一些宏观背景的人来说，有更多的自由空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll just be empowered to do more and more things.
zh: 他们将只是被赋能去做越来越多的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Two and a half years ago, I had this post I put out where I said, "Why PMs are the best positioned role in tech to thrive in an AI world."
zh: 两年半前，我发了一个帖子，我说，“为什么 PM 是科技中最有潜力在 AI 世界中蓬勃发展的角色。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And I feel like, even though the beginning of our conversation was like we should live in a world where we regret PM exists, I feel like we agree on this idea that the skills that seem to matter most and are going to be most valuable, whether it's a PM doing them or an engineer or designer, is very PM-y skills.
zh: 我觉得，尽管我们对话的开始就像是我们应该生活在一个后悔 PM 存在的世界里，我觉得我们在这一点上达成一致，即看起来最重要且将最有价值的技能，无论是 PM 还是工程师或设计师在做，都是非常 PM 式的技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll share a few examples from this post.
zh: 我会从这个帖子分享几个例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who is really good at this stuff, these things?
zh: 谁真的擅长这些东西，这些事？

speaker: Unknown
en: Identifying what to build, distilling, communicating requirements, prioritizing everyone's ideas for the highest ROI opportunities, giving feedback and design to improve impact, developing go-to-market strategy, understanding business strategy.
zh: 识别要构建什么，提炼和传达需求，将每个人的想法按最高 ROI 机会进行优先级排序，提供设计和反馈以改善影响力，制定上市策略，理解业务战略。

speaker: Unknown
en: To me, this is what PMs do, and it feels like that's becoming more and more important.
zh: 对我来说，这就是 PM 所做的，感觉这变得越来越重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I guess the question to you is, would you agree with this idea that the PME skills seem to be the most valuable now as AI takes on the building?
zh: 所以我想问你的问题是，你同意这个想法吗，即 PM 技能似乎是最有价值的，因为 AI 接管了构建工作？

speaker: Unknown
en: Definitely agree.
zh: 绝对同意。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also props for bringing in the receipts even with a timestamp, my friend.
zh: 也赞扬一下带着证据甚至带时间戳这件事，我的朋友。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well done.
zh: 干得好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think my only build on that would be to say I think those core PM skills aren't necessarily the things that we have rewarded PMs for over the last five years, versus storytelling, alignment, strategy.
zh: 我对此唯一的补充是，我认为这些核心 PM 技能不一定是我们在过去五年中奖励 PM 的东西，相比之下讲故事、对齐、战略才是。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I do think you're 100% correct that can I genuinely understand the customer?
zh: 所以我确实认为你 100% 正确，那就是我能否真正理解客户？

speaker: Unknown
en: Can I genuinely understand the business?
zh: 我能否真正理解业务？

speaker: Unknown
en: Can I genuinely understand the tech?
zh: 我能否真正理解技术？

speaker: Unknown
en: And can I translate the three together for optimal efficiency, is the point of leverage when doing things gets cheaper, trying things is cheaper, et cetera.
zh: 我能否将这三者结合起来以实现最优效率，这才是做事变便宜、试错成本变低等情况下的杠杆点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So absolutely agree that product skills are probably the most durable.
zh: 所以完全认同产品技能可能是最持久的。

speaker: Unknown
en: My build would just be there's a lot of people who have the title PM who haven't spent a lot of time building those skills in the last five years, but have gotten really good at communicating frameworks to leadership.
zh: 我的补充观点是，有很多人拥有 PM 这个头衔，但在过去五年里没有花太多时间构建这些技能，却非常擅长向领导层传达框架。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I just kind of push us back as a function into that core work.
zh: 所以我只是想让我们作为一个职能回归到那项核心工作中去。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Marty Cagan calls this product theater.
zh: Marty Cagan 称之为产品剧场。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of people just do the things that PMs should be doing.
zh: 很多人只是做 PM 应该做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And listen, I'm guilty of this.
zh: 听着，我也对此有愧疚。

speaker: Unknown
en: We rewarded it for so long that it doesn't surprise me that that product theater is a core skillset for a lot of folks.
zh: 我们长期奖励这种行为，以至于我不惊讶产品剧场已经成为许多人的核心技能组合。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just think that there's not a lot of place to hide in that anymore.
zh: 我只是认为那里已经没有太多可以躲藏的地方了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this comes back to that 32,000 people applied for jobs.
zh: 这又回到了那 32,000 人申请工作的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I imagine a lot of that is just people who think they're PMs, or have the title PM, but are exactly what you described.
zh: 我想象其中很多只是那些自认为是 PM，或者拥有 PM 头衔，但完全是你所描述的那种人。

speaker: Unknown
en: They just focus a lot on alignment, writing docs, meetings, things like that, and not actual building, understanding what it takes to build a successful product.
zh: 他们只是非常专注于对齐、写文档、开会之类的事情，而不是实际的构建，理解构建成功产品所需要的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The number of people who do really well in a product interview, Lenny, and then you give them a case study.
zh: 有很多人在产品面试中表现非常出色，Lenny，然后你给他们一个案例研究。

speaker: Unknown
en: So everyone who gets hired at Whatnot in any role has to do an actual hands-on case study.
zh: 所以每个在 Whatnot 被录用任何角色的人都必须做一个实际动手的案例研究。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the number of people who present incredibly well, and then you give them a prompt and some data, and ask them to come back with a POV on something, and then we make them verbally defend it, how quickly the thinking decays from folks who are good at the theater, but not the specifics is really telling, I think.
zh: 但是那些表现得令人难以置信的人的数量，当你给他们一个提示和一些数据，并要求他们带回一个观点，然后我们让他们口头辩护时，对于那些擅长剧场但不懂细节的人来说，他们的思维退化得有多快，我觉得真的很说明问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So going beyond the hiring step, say you hire somebody, what are some things you've learned about how to get the most out of the people you hire?
zh: 所以超越招聘这一步，假设你雇了某人，关于如何从你雇用的人身上获得最大收益，你学到了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: You mentioned this kind of contrarian take that you don't agree with this hire great people, get out of their way.
zh: 你提到了这种反向的观点，你不同意这种雇佣优秀的人，然后别挡他们的道。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I want to hear more about that.
zh: 所以我想多听听这方面的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: And just is there anything else you've learned about just elements to building your very successful world-class product team?
zh: 此外，关于构建你非常成功的世界级产品团队的要素，你还学到了其他什么吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, nuance required, in my life, hire people and get out of the way is wrong, I will say.
zh: 我的意思是，需要细微差别，在我的生活中，雇佣人然后别挡道是错误的，我会这么说。

speaker: Unknown
en: But couple of pieces to build off of it.
zh: 但有几个部分可以在此基础上展开。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think in general, the hire great people and get out of their way became this kind of macro saying for let them work out what the roadmap is, let them work out what the problems are, just completely devolve what's going on.
zh: 我认为总的来说，雇佣优秀的人然后别挡道变成了一种宏观说法，即让他们弄清楚路线图是什么，让他们弄清楚问题是什么，完全下放正在发生的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the real answer is obviously the better people you hire, the more you can totally trust that they know what they're doing.
zh: 我认为真正的答案显然是，你雇的人越好，你就越能完全信任他们知道自己在做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we tend to live in a verify, then trust land as opposed to a totally trust or even trust but verify, which is like I'm probably in a better position than any of my directs to understand how all of the different pieces of our system, buyer, seller, trust, fit together.
zh: 但我们倾向于生活在先验证再信任的土地上，而不是完全信任甚至信任但验证，这就像我可能比我的任何直属下级都处于更好的位置来理解我们系统的所有不同部分，买家、卖家、信任，是如何组合在一起的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're almost certainly in a better position than me to understand the nuance of how any of those individual features work.
zh: 他们几乎肯定比我处于更好的位置，以理解这些个别功能中的任何一个如何运作的细微差别。

speaker: Unknown
en: If somebody quizzed me today on exactly all the weightings in the Whatnot discovery model, I would definitely be wrong vis-a-vis any of the engineers on that team, vis-a-vis any of the PMs on that team.
zh: 如果有人今天考我 Whatnot 发现模型中所有的权重，我肯定会错的，相对于那个团队上的任何工程师，相对于那个团队上的任何 PM。

speaker: Unknown
en: Good.
zh: 很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's actually kind of incumbent on me to learn that and understand that over time because I'm asking them to make decisions, and I am proving things that they're doing.
zh: 但实际上我有责任随着时间的推移学习和理解这一点，因为我要求他们做出决策，而我在验证他们正在做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so time spent actually working alongside those teams in the trenches trying to solve something, really, really powerful.
zh: 所以花时间实际上与这些团队在战壕中并肩工作试图解决某事，真的非常强大。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the things that I saw earliest when I joined Whatnot that I've seen, Grant, who's our founder CEO do, is he'll sit in a review and be like, "I don't think this is right."
zh: 我加入 Whatnot 时最早看到的一件事，我看到我们的创始人 CEO Grant 做，是他会坐在评审中并说，“我不认为这是对的。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And then he'll pause and say, "I'm going to clear the rest of my day.
zh: 然后他会停顿说，“我要清理我这一天的其余时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's sit and figure it out."
zh: 让我们坐下来弄清楚。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And he'll actually end up sitting with the team and going through, again, easier with AI data tools, let's literally pull up the tickets.
zh: 他实际上会最终与团队坐在一起，再次，有了 AI 数据工具更容易，让我们真的拉起工单。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's literally pull up the code.
zh: 让我们真的拉起代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's go through the data line by line and understand what's actually happening so that we can make a decision there.
zh: 让我们逐行浏览数据并理解实际发生了什么，以便我们可以做出决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it means he's very up-to-date with what's going on, very culturally sets the tone for the team that we're just seeking truth.
zh: 这意味着他与正在发生的事情非常同步，在文化上为团队定下了基调，我们只是在寻求真相。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it makes it very much a us versus you.
zh: 这使得它非常变成一种我们与你们对立的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: Reviews got very into listen for yes for a little while there where all you're trying to do as a PM is just get a green light so that you can go back to your engineers and say, "I have some credibility.
zh: 评审有一段时间变得非常倾向于“听是为了说是”，你作为 PM 所做的一切就是试图得到绿灯，这样你就可以回到你的工程师那里说，“我有一些可信度。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can get the CPO to approve what we're building."
zh: 我可以让 CPO 批准我们正在构建的东西。”

speaker: Unknown
en: As opposed to this idea that says we're just trying to find out the right answer, and in theory, everyone wants us to come up with the right answer.
zh: 而不是这种观念，说我们只是试图找到正确的答案，理论上，每个人都希望我们得出正确的答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we use planning to align the company on what are the really important things we have to solve.
zh: 所以我们利用规划来使公司对齐我们必须解决的真正重要的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's mostly a resourcing discussion.
zh: 这主要是一个资源讨论。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we pick the right things, stack rank them all.
zh: 如果我们选择了正确的事情，按优先级排列它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ultimately, I'm most accountable for making sure that we have the right resources in the right places to hit things.
zh: 最终，我最负责任的是确保我们在正确的位置有正确的资源来达成目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I don't know if those are the right places if all I do is delegate to the team to go figure it out, and I'm not actually periodically very deep with them on exactly how does that work?
zh: 但我不知道那些是不是合适的地方，如果我做的只是把任务委派给团队去弄清楚，而我实际上并没有周期性地与他们深入探讨这究竟是如何运作的？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do our referrals work?
zh: 我们的推荐人是如何工作的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Literally, what is the logic that fraud might use in order to invalidate one?
zh: 字面意思就是，欺诈可能会使用什么逻辑来使一个推荐人无效？

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, based on address signals.
zh: 哦，基于地址信号。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we calculate address signals?
zh: 我们如何计算地址信号？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that a Google normalized thing, or is that free text that's put in?
zh: 那是谷歌归一化的东西，还是输入的自由文本？

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you don't actually push yourself down to sit alongside your IC engineers and your IC designers and your ICPMs, you don't actually know that stuff.
zh: 如果你不强迫自己坐下来，与你的 IC 工程师、IC 设计师和 ICPMs 并肩工作，你实际上并不了解那些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can't make good macro decisions without the micro.
zh: 所以如果没有微观基础，你就无法做出好的宏观决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: So increasingly, I think I push myself to I try and be T-shaped.
zh: 所以越来越多地，我试图推动自己成为 T 型人才。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can go very, very deep when required, but I'm mostly broad across pieces.
zh: 我可以在需要时变得非常、非常深入，但我主要是广泛涉猎各个领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the idea of just hiring people, and then not asking any more questions and delegating all of the detail just isn't really the most successful model for getting the most out of an organization.
zh: 我认为只是雇佣人员，然后不再问任何问题并委派所有细节，实际上并不是从组织中获得最大收益的最成功模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: With a very product-minded founder, CPO classically is a very challenging role for people because you're basically this person between a very opinionated founder and the team building it.
zh: 对于一位非常有产品思维的的创始人来说，CPO 经典来说对人们来说是一个非常具有挑战性的角色，因为你基本上就是处于这位非常有主见的创始人和构建它的团队之间的这个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: What have you found works in creating an environment where you are happy in that role?
zh: 你发现什么方法在创造一个让你在这个角色中感到愉快的环境方面是有效的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Funnily, that's become most of my career.
zh: 有趣的是，这已经成为了我职业生涯的大部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Actually, I've worked for three founders in a row who are all very product-minded and whatnot.
zh: 实际上，我连续为三位非常具有产品思维等等的创始人工作过。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've got two, which is a blessing actually.
zh: 我现在有两位，这实际上是一种福气。

speaker: Unknown
en: In general, I try not to double up.
zh: 总的来说，我尽量避免重复。

speaker: Unknown
en: If Grant or Logan, our founders are on a thing, probably doesn't need me.
zh: 如果 Grant 或 Logan，我们的创始人正在处理某件事，可能并不需要我。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the advantage of an extra layer?
zh: 增加一个额外层级的优势是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think jokingly one of the PMs on the team has referred to it as the two dads problem where you've just got two people issuing conflicting instructions, or somebody wants to review and then you do all this work to present it to me, and then you go back and it gets a different thing.
zh: 我想开玩笑地说，团队中的一位 PM 曾经称之为“两个爸爸”的问题，就是你刚刚有两个人发出相互冲突的指令，或者某人想要审查，然后你做了所有这些工作把它展示给我，然后你回去又得到了一个不同的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So my first thing is if Grant or Logan are on it, I check that they're watching it, they're accountable for it, and I step out.
zh: 所以我的第一件事是，如果 Grant 或 Logan 在处理这件事，我会确认他们在盯着它，他们对此负责，然后我就退出。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there'll be long periods of time where fully half my team can be working on something, and I couldn't tell you day-to-day where it is because it's with Grant, it's with Logan, and that's totally fine.
zh: 所以会有很长的一段时间，我团队的一半人都在做某件事，而我无法告诉你每天它的进展如何，因为它和 Grant 在一起，它和 Logan 在一起，这完全没问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't have to be across all of the things they're doing.
zh: 我不必了解他们正在做的所有事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just need to make sure that there is somebody doing that bar raising.
zh: 我们只需要确保有一个人在做那个提高标准的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we spent much time doing that alignment.
zh: 所以我们花了很多时间做这种对齐。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the second one is, ultimately, if you are a product leader in a founder-led company, you have to understand it's not your company, it's theirs.
zh: 我认为第二点是，归根结底，如果你是一家创始人领导的公司中的产品负责人，你必须明白这不是你的公司，是他们的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you just find the right balance of, hey, are you open to feedback on this?
zh: 你只需要找到正确的平衡点，嘿，你对接受这个问题的反馈持开放态度吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Have you made up your mind?
zh: 你已经下定决心了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you open to a push on this?
zh: 你对这个问题的推进持开放态度吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And you just find that rhythm working with folks.
zh: 你只需在与人们合作时找到那种节奏。

speaker: Unknown
en: Generally speaking, there's a reason that founder-led companies do so well in our industry.
zh: 一般来说，创始人领导的公司在我们的行业做得这么好是有原因的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The insight required and the kind of customer intuition to make the thing in the first place and work tends to be really important.
zh: 所需的洞察力，以及为了从头开始制造这个东西和工作所需的客户直觉，往往非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I just view my job as making sure that we've got coverage on the places where our founders are.
zh: 然后我只是将我的工作视为确保我们能覆盖到我们创始人所在的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: Awesome.
zh: 太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a couple things you've learned here for building, and I think in consumer, this is especially important, is counterintuitively to how maybe people think things should work, you're finding that the best teams, companies, products end up coming from top-down, founder-led, almost micromanagement is a dirty word to a lot of people, but it's basically being in the weeds is, in spite of how people may feel, this actually ends up being leading to better stuff, better [inaudible 00:55:56].
zh: 所以关于构建你在这里学到的几件事，我认为在消费领域，这尤其重要，这与人们可能认为事情应该如何运作的直觉相反，你发现最好的团队、公司、产品最终来自自上而下、创始人主导的，微管理对很多人来说是一个肮脏的词，但这基本上就是深入细节，尽管人们可能有这种感觉，这实际上最终会导致更好的东西，更好的 [听不清 00:55:56]。

speaker: Unknown
en: Top-down works well if leadership is good enough to be in the weeds and be specifically correct.
zh: 如果领导层足够优秀，能够深入细节并做到具体正确，那么自上而下就运作良好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think where it falls apart is where you don't actually know ground truth and then you attempt to manage people from above.
zh: 我认为它破裂的地方在于，你实际上并不了解事实真相，然后你试图从上面管理人员。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's where I think the term micromanagement comes from.
zh: 我认为这就是微管理这个术语的来源。

speaker: Unknown
