en: Otherwise, if you're working from the same data and you have it, I don't know a junior engineer or an entry-level designer who isn't stoked to sit there and work alongside the CPO or the CEO and ship something because you're just unblocked.
zh: 否则，如果你基于相同的数据工作并且你拥有这些数据，我不知道有哪个初级工程师或入门级设计师会不愿意坐在那里与 CPO 或 CEO 并肩工作并发布东西，因为你只是没有被阻碍。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no alignment meetings, there's nothing to do.
zh: 没有对齐会议，没有什么可做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I also find that you can give way better feedback if you're literally in the detail.
zh: 我还发现，如果你真的在细节中，你可以给出更好的反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the nuance is just like, how do you make sure you can do that in enough places?
zh: 我认为细微差别就像，你如何确保你可以在足够多的地方做到这一点？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's never been a better time to attempt to be in the detail on things because you can literally query it in real time.
zh: 尝试在事情上深入细节从未有过比现在更好的时机，因为你实际上可以实时查询它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's such an important nuance here.
zh: 我认为这里有一个非常重要的细微差别。

speaker: Unknown
en: The story told is so powerful, this idea of Grant just, okay, I'm going to clear my day.
zh: 讲述的故事是如此强大，Grant 的这个想法，好的，我要清理我的一天。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to spend time going deep on this stuff.
zh: 我要花时间深入研究这些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: That feels like a very necessary ingredient for someone at the top to be making micro decisions.
zh: 这似乎是高层人士做出微观决策的一个非常必要的成分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because to your point, if they don't have all the details, they're not making a decision out of real data.
zh: 因为正如你的观点，如果他们没有掌握所有细节，他们就不是根据真实数据做出决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we can do that because, as I said, we plan what we're doing and then we allocate, and then we're dividing and conquering.
zh: 我们可以这样做，因为正如我所说，我们计划我们要做的事情，然后我们进行分配，然后我们正在分而治之。

speaker: Unknown
en: So he's probably trying to nail three or four most important things at a time.
zh: 所以他可能正试图一次敲定三或四件最重要的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he's the CEO.
zh: 而他是 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's going to call the ball and say, these are the four things I own right now.
zh: 他会做出决断并说，这就是我现在负责的四件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm going to be like, "Great, I'll be over here then."
zh: 而我会说，「好的，那我就待在这儿。」

speaker: Unknown
en: And then within those, what am I doing with the rest of my day that is more important than nailing the five things I've said we'll get done this half?
zh: 然后在这些事情中，我在这一天的剩余时间里要做什么，比搞定我所说的我们在这一半时间会完成的五件事更重要呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: If it's anything other than maybe hiring, standing meetings, any of that stuff, you can just clear it and set the tone for the team that until we understand it, we can't do anything else.
zh: 如果不是招聘、例会之类的事情，你就可以直接把它清理掉，并为团队定下基调，直到我们理解了它，否则我们不能做其他任何事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Say somebody is looking for a CPO role or a first PM role, they're kind of similar, basically working for a founder.
zh: 比如说有人正在寻找 CPO 职位或者第一个 PM 角色，它们有点相似，基本上是为创始人工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: What would be your advice for them to land in a place where they're happy and not just super frustrated by this kind of middle layer where they just don't actually have any agency?
zh: 对于他们来说，要想落脚在一个他们会感到快乐，而不是仅仅被这种他们实际上没有任何主观能动性的中间层搞得超级沮丧的地方，你有什么建议？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean, I think the first thing you've got to work out is why do you want it?
zh: 是的，我的意思是，我认为你必须弄清楚的第一件事就是你为什么想要它？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's this idea that the CPO's job, you get to decide all the roadmaps and all those things, and I've got bad news for you.
zh: 有这样一种观念，认为 CPO 的工作，你可以决定所有的路线图和所有这些事情，而我要给你带来坏消息。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's not strictly true.
zh: 这并不完全是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think it also comes down to spending some time with that person to work out how do we jam on a topic?
zh: 但我认为这也归结为花时间和那个人在一起，弄清楚我们在一个主题上如何即兴协作？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do they like to get pushed?
zh: 他们喜欢怎么被推动？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do they not?
zh: 又不喜欢怎么被推动？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you spend a lot of your time calibrating.
zh: 然后你会花很多时间进行校准。

speaker: Unknown
en: So before I joined Whatnot, I think Grant and I had five or six different coffees where we talked about how do you get this type of team to move?
zh: 所以在我加入 Whatnot 之前，我想 Grant 和我大概喝过五或六次不同的咖啡，我们谈论了如何让这类团队运转起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you work on those things?
zh: 你们如何处理这些事情？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I obviously went through a series of interviews, and actually came down to LA where Grant and Logan were based at the time, and spent a whole day with them just in a room, going through a couple different problems, talking through different things in the roadmap, just really getting into it.
zh: 然后我显然经历了一系列面试，实际上去了洛杉矶，Grant 和 Logan 当时就在那里，和他们花了一整天时间待在一个房间里，过了一两个不同的问题，讨论路线图中的不同事情，真的深入其中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I tried through that to be my most ordinary self as opposed to interview self, if that makes sense.
zh: 而且我试图通过这个过程展示我最真实的一面，而不是面试时的那一面，如果这说得通的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because you got to ask yourself, do I really want to spend my whole time having this discussion and this debate?
zh: 因为你得问问自己，我真的想花我的所有时间进行这种讨论和辩论吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: But I like being a CPO or a product lead because in a lot of ways what I'm doing is I'm helping translate that vision and that intuition into reality.
zh: 但我喜欢做 CPO 或产品负责人，因为在很多方面，我所做的是在帮助将那个愿景和直觉转化为现实。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there is an art to learning how to push somebody without competing with them.
zh: 然后有一种艺术，就是学习如何在不与某人竞争的情况下推动他。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think a lot of the times I've seen the CPO CEO relationship go badly.
zh: 我认为很多时候我看到 CPO 和 CEO 的关系变得很糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: It ends up with the CPO is competing with the CEO for vision and they end up at loggerheads.
zh: 最终变成了 CPO 在愿景上与 CEO 竞争，而且他们陷入了僵局。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's not your job.
zh: 我认为那不是你的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to ask more about that, this art of pushing back and nudging things in a direction.
zh: 我想多问问关于那个，这种回击和向某个方向推动事情的艺术。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there one trick or one tip you might share with folks to be good at... Because a lot of people deal with execs and they're always trying to get them to agree to what they want.
zh: 有没有什么一个技巧或一条建议你可能会分享给大家来做到擅长……因为很多人与高管打交道，他们总是试图让高管同意他们想要的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the first thing is don't treat it as a trick.
zh: 我认为第一件事是不要把它当作一个技巧。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you're not trying to get an answer and a yes.
zh: 我的意思是，你不是试图得到一个答案和一个肯定。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're trying to seek truth is my first statement.
zh: 你是在寻求真理，这是我的第一点陈述。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I wouldn't say it's especially common that we start out of alignment, but I do think, part of your role, if you're one of the more senior product folks in the room and the CEO, or if you're a director and it's the CPO in the room, is pushing the team in a way that you don't really expect or you don't really understand, is start from a place of curiosity.
zh: 所以我不会说我们从一开始就不一致这特别常见，但我确实认为，如果你是房间里级别较高的产品人员之一，而 CEO 也在场，或者如果你是一名总监而 CPO 在场，你角色的一部分就是以一种你并不真正期待或并不真正理解的方式推动团队，就是从好奇心的地方开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: Does that person have more context than you or is there a thing that you're not aware of that is guiding it?

zh: 你真的永远不会关闭商店，因为这种客流远超你想象中在商店里的人数，因为商业的经济模式与娱乐完全不同，而且你不需要担心千次展示成本（CPM）。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think it's not really in competition with agentic.
zh: 所以我认为它真的不是与智能体竞争。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's a completely different customer need.
zh: 我认为这是一种完全不同的客户需求。

speaker: Unknown
en: Amazing.
zh: 太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's room for everyone.
zh: 每个人都有空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to end maybe with a question about Twitter.
zh: 我想最后也许问一个关于 Twitter 的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you were a Twitter.
zh: 所以你是 Twitter 的。

speaker: Tom Verrilli
en: Yes, sir.
zh: 是的，先生。

speaker: Unknown
en: A PM at Twitter working on growth.
zh: 一位在 Twitter 负责增长的 PM。

speaker: Unknown
en: I feel like everybody that worked at Twitter as a PM was just scarred from the experience of Twitter.
zh: 我觉得每一个在 Twitter 当过 PM 的人都只是被 Twitter 的经历留下了心理阴影。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone said, "Do not do things this way."
zh: 每个人都说，“不要这样做事。”

speaker: Unknown
en: What's something that stuck with you from that experience?
zh: 那段经历中有什么东西让你印象深刻？

speaker: Unknown
en: What did you learn?
zh: 你学到了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What did you unlearn?
zh: 你摒弃了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: It is funny.
zh: 这很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have said to a friend before that asking someone who was at Twitter in the 2015, '16 era is a little bit like a therapist asking somebody to tell them about their childhood.
zh: 我以前对一位朋友说过，问一个在 2015、2016 年代在 Twitter 的人，有点像治疗师让人讲述他们的童年。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like you know the trauma that you're bringing up.
zh: 就像你知道你正在提起的创伤。

speaker: Unknown
en: For those who are not familiar with that lore, I think we had nine heads of product in the two years that I was there.
zh: 对于那些不熟悉那段传说的人来说，我想我在那里的两年里，我们换了九任产品负责人。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was that level of kind of chaos.
zh: 就是那种程度的混乱。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think my favorite quote was from someone on the partnerships team who said it felt like Kara Swisher lived in the air vents.
zh: 我想我最喜欢的一句引语来自合作团队的一位人士，他说感觉像是 Kara Swisher 住在通风管道里。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was how often drama was going on about the place.
zh: 这就是那个地方发生戏剧性事件的频率。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think, Lenny, I probably took two overwhelming things away from my time at Twitter.
zh: 我想，Lenny，我可能从我在 Twitter 的时光中带走了两件压倒性的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And other than some incredible friends, and I will say that the product diaspora from that era of Twitter is pretty incredible and everywhere.
zh: 除了一些不可思议的朋友之外，我想说那个时代的 Twitter 产品散居群体相当不可思议，而且无处不在。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first one is if you truly find product market fit, if you manage to bottle lightning, doesn't matter how badly you screw up the organization of it.
zh: 第一件是，如果你真的找到了产品市场契合度（PMF），如果你成功地将闪电装进瓶子里，无论你把组织搞得多么糟糕都不重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's huge.
zh: 它很巨大。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Twitter genuinely had that level of product market fit that you could emotionally feel how much people loved your product.
zh: Twitter 确实拥有那种程度的产品市场契合度，你可以情感上感受到人们有多么热爱你的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's a really powerful litmus test to learn relatively early in your career that that's what PMF is.
zh: 在你的职业生涯早期就能学到这一点，这是一个非常强大的试金石，可以让你明白什么是 PMF。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not like, hey, the graphs look okay.
zh: 不像，嘿，图表看起来还可以。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a level of fervor that goes in.
zh: 其中投入了一定程度的狂热。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think maybe on the flip side of less positive is what it definitely learned is most of the time you hear it's really complex, it isn't.
zh: 我想也许在不太积极的一面是，我确实学到的是，大多数时候当你听说它真的很复杂时，它其实并不复杂。

speaker: Unknown
en: Leadership's just weak.
zh: 只是领导力太弱了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the two years that I was there, everyone knew we were going to have to lift the 140 character limit.
zh: 所以我在那里的那两年，每个人都知道我们将不得不提高 140 个字符的限制。

speaker: Unknown
en: There was working group after working group.
zh: 一个又一个工作组。

speaker: Unknown
en: The project beyond 140 was everywhere.
zh: “超越 140”的项目随处可见。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because we knew, for example, that people in Japan Tweeted six times more often than people in Western markets.
zh: 因为我们要知道，例如，在日本发推特的人比西方市场的人发推特频率高出六倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was largely when we spoke to them because Kanji lets you say heaps more in the same number of characters than a romance language did.
zh: 当我们与他们交谈时很大程度上是因为，汉字让你在相同数量的字符里比罗曼语族语言表达多得多的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: We knew that was the inevitable end state, but there's obviously a bunch of work that was needed and trade-offs, and just no one wanted to make the call.
zh: 我们知道那是必然的最终状态，但显然需要做大量的工作和权衡，只是没有人愿意做出决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there was just yet another design sprint, yet another cycle.
zh: 所以只是又一次设计冲刺，又一个循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was another year and a half after I left, I think it was maybe even almost two years after I left, before someone actually did it.
zh: 在我离开后又是一年半的时间，我想那可能甚至是在我离开后差不多两年，才有人真正去做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it turns out nobody died.
zh: 结果没人死掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: The soul of the place didn't fall apart.
zh: 这个地方的灵魂没有分崩离析。

speaker: Unknown
en: I imagine the same discussion went on for editing Tweets, which took another two and a half years.
zh: 我想象关于编辑推文的讨论也是一样的，这又花了两年半的时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes things aren't actually that complicated.
zh: 有时候事情实际上没那么复杂。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just weak leadership.
zh: 只是领导力软弱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it's funny how far it's come.
zh: 是啊，它发展到这一步真是有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now you can write entire blog posts on Twitter.
zh: 现在你可以在 Twitter 上写整篇博客文章了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Articles is a big bet.
zh: 文章功能是一个大赌注。

speaker: Unknown
en: On the product market fit piece, I think even more important there is the network effects of a Twitter, which you spend a lot of time thinking about building marketplaces.
zh: 在产品市场契合度方面，我认为更重要的是 Twitter 的网络效应，你花了大量时间思考建立市场的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: To me, watching Elon basically change everything, I forget who Tweeted this, but just everything changed.
zh: 对我来说，看着 Elon 基本上改变了一切，我忘了是谁发推文说的，但一切都变了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The brand, the name, the website.
zh: 品牌、名字、网站。

speaker: Unknown
en: Number of people working there, everything.
zh: 在那里工作的人数，一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, the people, the team.
zh: 是的，人，团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: What was the thing that stayed the same?
zh: 什么东西保持不变了？

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was basically the network effects of Twitter.
zh: 基本上是 Twitter 的网络效应。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the place to be, so everyone's there.
zh: 那个地方才是归属之地，所以每个人都在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's hard to break.
zh: 而这很难打破。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even in spite of how much he tried to mess it all up, it's still kicking.
zh: 尽管他多么努力想把它搞砸，它仍然在运转。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's it.
zh: 就是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you bottle lightning, genuinely you can tell.
zh: 如果你装瓶抓住了闪电，真的你能看出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to take us to a recurring corner of the podcast, Fail Corner.
zh: 我要带我们去播客的一个常驻环节，失败角。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why I like doing this is because people see people like you coming on the podcast, have this illustrious career, everything's going great constantly, you're just killing it.
zh: 我喜欢做这个是因为人们看到像你这样的人来到播客，拥有辉煌的职业生涯，一切都在不断变好，你只是在赢。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they don't see the things that don't work out and the times that you failed.
zh: 而他们看不到那些没做成的事情和你失败的时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in their life, things often go wrong.
zh: 而在他们的生活中，事情经常出错。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the question for you is just what's an example of a time in your career where things failed, something you built, some career move you made that didn't work out, and then what'd you learn from that experience?
zh: 所以给你的问题是，就在你职业生涯中某个失败时刻的例子，你建立的东西，你做出的职业变动没有成功，然后你从那次经历中学到了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Honestly, mate, and it's very nice of you to say nice things, but I feel like I fail more often than I succeed across the course of my career.
zh: 老实说，伙计，你说好话真是太好了，但我觉得我在我的职业生涯中失败比成功更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Genuinely, to the blog you referenced right at the start, I published in the back of that the actual document we use internally to talk about how we build.
zh: 真的，关于你最开始引用的那篇博客，我在那篇博客的后面发布了一份我们内部实际使用的文件，用来讨论我们是如何构建的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it starts with batting .500 is the goal.
zh: 它从“打击率 0.500 是目标”开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're hoping to be right as often as you're wrong.
zh: 所以你希望对错参半，你做对的次数和你做错的次数一样多。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's probably just too many specific examples of times I've screwed up in my career, but there probably is a really common thread to it.
zh: 所以在我的职业生涯中可能我搞砸的具体例子太多了，但这其中可能真的有一个共同的线索。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's probably an easy trap for any PM to fall into, which is averages mean nothing to the individual is probably the thing that I've really scarred by.
zh: 我认为这可能是任何 PM 都容易陷入的一个简单陷阱，即“平均值对个人毫无意义”，这可能是我真正深受其害的一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: In any sizable population, it's really attractive to go and look at average utility or average adoption of something.
zh: 在任何相当大的人群中，去查看平均效用或某样东西的平均采用率是非常有吸引力的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you find that only 3% of people use something.
zh: 然后你会发现只有 3% 的人在使用某样东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you're like, "Cool, we can probably get rid of that feature.
zh: 然后你会说，“酷，我们可能可以去掉那个功能。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not used widely."
zh: 它没有被广泛使用。”

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you don't go a layer deeper, and be like, actually it's only 3% of something, but there's a group of people for whom it's 100% of what they do.
zh: 但如果你不深挖一层，去发现实际上虽然只是某样东西的 3%，但对于一群人来说这是他们所做事情的 100%。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is their core use case.
zh: 这是他们的核心用例。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for expediency's sake, because somebody doesn't want to maintain a feature anymore, you're just going to deprecate it.
zh: 为了图省事，因为有人不想再维护某个功能了，你只是要去弃用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it turns out you blow up the use case of that group of humans.
zh: 结果你搞炸了这群人的用例。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then to your last point about network effects, the ongoing spiral effect of that can be enormous.
zh: 然后关于你刚才关于网络效应的最后一点，由此产生的持续螺旋效应可能是巨大的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think about it a lot in e-commerce of this is somebody's business.
zh: 在电商方面我经常想这个问题，这是某人的生意。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we're just not reliable or we're deprecating a feature, it's kind of like a Westfield Mall just turning off the power in the lead up to Christmas without thinking about it.
zh: 如果我们只是不可靠或者我们在弃用一个功能，这就像 Westfield 购物中心在圣诞节前夕没有多想就切断了电源。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there are real downstream impacts to people's businesses that often come from just a lack of nuance in understanding metrics, particularly averages.
zh: 所以对人们的生意有真正的下游影响，这通常来自于对指标缺乏细致的理解，特别是平均值。

speaker: Unknown
en: They just lie to you all the time.
zh: 它们总是对你撒谎。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think I've probably screwed up in all of the ways in my career, but most of the time I've made genuinely I'm disappointed in myself levels of decisions, it's typically that I've relied on averages without thinking about the individual use cases that are hidden underneath.
zh: 我想我在我的职业生涯中可能搞砸了所有的方式，但大多数时候我做出了真正让自己感到失望级别的决定，通常是因为我依赖了平均值，而没有考虑隐藏在底下的个人用例。

speaker: Unknown
en: Makes me think about Jeff Bezos has a quote, "When you have data and an anecdote, trust the anecdote."
zh: 这让我想到了 Jeff Bezos 的一句话，“当你有数据和轶事时，相信轶事。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, that's exactly right.
zh: 是的，完全正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, Tom, we've gone through everything I wanted to talk about.
zh: 好吧，Tom，我们已经聊完了我想谈论的所有事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there anything else that you wanted to share?
zh: 还有什么你想分享的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Anything you want to leave listeners with before we get to a very exciting lightning round?
zh: 在我们进入非常激动人心的快问快答环节之前，你想给听众留下些什么吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think all I'd add, mate, I've really enjoyed the discussion, so thank you, is like-
zh: 我想我想补充的就是，伙计，我真的很享受这次讨论，所以谢谢你，就像——

speaker: Lenny
en: Same.
zh: 我也一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think there is one way to do product management, and I don't think there is one way that AI will shape the industry.
zh: 我认为做产品管理没有一种唯一的方法，我认为 AI 塑造这个行业也没有一种唯一的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're pretty confident that for Whatnot, the product we're building and the culture of the company that we have, that this model of fewer PMs who are more senior with a lot more autonomy is right for us.
zh: 所以我们非常有信心，对于 Whatnot，我们要构建的产品以及我们拥有的公司文化，这种更资深、拥有更多自主权的 PM 更少的模式对我们来说是对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't pretend to presume that that will be true for the entire industry, but I do think there has never been a better time to go back to the roots of the actual product work and getting out of that theater.
zh: 我不假装这对整个行业都适用，但我确实认为，回归到实际产品工作的根源并摆脱那种「剧场」模式，从来没有比现在更好的时机了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that probably is true everywhere, even if you are still, there are people who are wonderful people managers and really derive their satisfaction from doing that and growing and coaching.
zh: 我认为这在各地可能都是真的，即使你仍然……有些人是很棒的人员管理者，并且真正从做这件事以及指导和成长中获得满足感。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm sure there'll be loads of places where that's still valuable.
zh: 我确信在很多地方这仍然是有价值的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So assume that at least half of what I've said is wrong in the same basis that half of the things I've probably ever shipped are not correct.
zh: 所以假设我说过的话里至少有一半是错的，基于同样的基础，我可能发布过的东西里有一半是不正确的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why I love these conversations, and why I think this work that we do together is important is we are living through the wildest time in our careers.
zh: 这就是为什么我喜欢这些对话，也是为什么我认为我们要一起做的这项工作很重要，是因为我们正在经历职业生涯中最疯狂的时期。

speaker: Unknown
en: So much is changing.
zh: 很多变革正在发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: So much is being rethought, as you've described.
zh: 正如你所描述的，很多事物正在被重新思考。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it feels like the only way we can make our way through this successfully is to learn from how other people are approaching it, see what they've learned, see what has not worked.
zh: 感觉我们要想成功度过这个时期，唯一的方法就是从别人如何处理这件事中学习，看看他们学到了什么，看看什么不起作用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Take bits that resonate, ignore the bits that seem bombastic or not applicable.
zh: 保留产生共鸣的部分，忽略那些看起来浮夸或不适用的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly.
zh: 确实如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because no one knows exactly where... Elizabeth Stone had this great way of putting it.
zh: 因为没有人确切地知道……Elizabeth Stone 有个很棒的说法。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a storming phase and the norming phase, and we're in the storming phase of holy shit.
zh: 有一个动荡期和一个规范期，而我们正处于「天哪这太疯狂了」的动荡期。

speaker: Unknown
en: I remember in my PM career, as I started writing and stuff, everyone's always asking me, "How has product management changed over the last decade?"
zh: 我记得在我的 PM 职业生涯中，当我开始写作之类的时候，大家总是问我，“在过去十年中产品管理发生了怎样的变化？”

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm like, "It hasn't changed.
zh: 我就说，“它没有变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the same basically."
zh: 基本上是一样的。”

speaker: Unknown
en: But it feels like now it actually has significantly changed, which feels weird.
zh: 但感觉像是现在它确实发生了显著变化，这感觉很奇怪。

speaker: Unknown
en: Although to your point earlier, actually the core things-
zh: 虽然就像你之前说的，实际上核心的东西——

speaker: Unknown
en: And also not.
zh: 而且也没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: ... will all be the same.
zh: ……都会是一样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's why these are so useful just for people to see here's how a team is operating and what they've learned, and here's things to try and it may not work for you.
zh: 所以这就是为什么这些对话非常有用，让人们可以看到这里有一个团队是如何运作的，他们学到了什么，这里有一些事情可以尝试，但可能对你不起作用。

speaker: Unknown
en: But this is how we learn from each other.
zh: 但这就是我们互相学习的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: With that, we have reached a very exciting lightning round.
zh: 既然如此，我们已经到了一个非常激动人心的快问快答环节。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've got five questions for you.
zh: 我有五个问题要问你。

speaker: Unknown
en: All right, here we go.
zh: 好吧，我们开始吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are two or three books that you find yourself recommending most to other people?
zh: 有哪两三本书是你发现自己最经常向其他人推荐的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not to be cliched, but The Hard Thing about Hard Things I still think is the best book written about product management, just from a breadth of things that you have to go through and try and do and screw up a lot.
zh: 虽然不想老生常谈，但我仍然认为《创业维艰》是关于产品管理写得最好的书，仅仅从你必须经历、尝试和搞砸的一系列事情来看。

speaker: Unknown
en: Slightly left field, but the best book anyone's ever recommended to me to read, which I now recommend to others, is The Purpose Driven Church by a pastor called Rick Warren.
zh: 有点偏门，但任何人推荐给我读过的最好的书，也就是我现在推荐给别人的，是一位名叫 Rick Warren 的牧师写的《标杆人生》。

speaker: Unknown
en: Emmett Shear, the CEO at Twitch, used to basically make sure that people read it.
zh: Twitch 的 CEO Emmett Shear 过去基本上会确保人们读过它。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's this wild examination of why people emotionally invest in something and how to engineer emotional investment into it from a group of people.
zh: 这是对人们为什么在情感上投入某事以及如何从一群人中为其设计情感投入的疯狂审视。
